column1: Manual Fact Display and Prediction
column29:
As a tagging user, I want manually added facts to appear with a distinct "Manual" badge and participate in AI prediction, so that they are treated equally in the tagging workflow.

 

Description: Manually added facts appear in the fact list with a purple "Manual" source badge, are included in prediction requests, and follow the same accept/reject/swap flow as AI-detected facts.
column363:
h3. AC8: Manual Source Badge

* Manually added facts display a purple "✋ Manual" source badge (purple-700 text, purple-50 background, purple-200 border).

* The badge is visually distinct from "⊞ Table" (sky/teal) and "¶ Narrative" (orange).

 

h3. AC9: Fact Type Auto-Classification

* Values containing $, £, €, or ¥ are classified as "monetary".

* Values containing % are classified as "percentage".

* Pure numeric values under 20 characters are classified as "monetary".

* All other values are classified as "text_block".

* The classification is reflected in the fact type badge (Monetary, %, Text Block).

 

h3. AC10: Filter Compatibility

* Manual facts appear when the source type filter is set to "All sources".

* Manual facts are hidden when the source type filter is set to "Table" or "Narrative" (they are neither).

* The fact type filter works correctly on manual facts based on their auto-classified type.

 

h3. AC11: Prediction Inclusion

* When the user clicks "Predict Tags", manual facts that are selected (isSelected: true) are included in the prediction request.

* The prediction engine returns element suggestions, confidence scores, reasoning, and alternatives for manual facts.

* Manual facts appear in the prediction review view with the same card format as AI-detected facts.

* Accept, reject, swap, edit, and undo operations work identically for manual facts.

column1: Add to Session from Document Selection
column29:
As a tagging user, I want to select content in the document and click "Add to Session" to add it as a manual fact, so that I can include missed content in the current AI tagging session.

 

Description: When manual fact addition mode is active, selecting content in the document shows a purple "Add to Session" button in the floating toolbar. Clicking it creates a new fact in the session with the selected content.
column363:
h3. AC4: Floating Toolbar — Narrative Selection

* When isAddingManualFact is true and the user selects narrative text by dragging, the floating toolbar shows only a purple "Add to Session" button.

* The "Mark as Fact", "Suggest tag with AI", and "Detect Facts" buttons are hidden.

* The toolbar container has a purple border (border-2 border-purple-300) to visually distinguish from the normal toolbar.

 

h3. AC5: Floating Toolbar — Table Cell Selection

* When isAddingManualFact is true and the user clicks a table cell, the floating toolbar shows "Add to Session" (purple) instead of "Detect Facts" (teal).

* The toolbar container has a purple border.

 

h3. AC6: Fact Creation on Click

* Clicking "Add to Session" creates a new DetectedFact with: unique ID (df-manual-{timestamp}-{random}), value from the selected text, sourceType "manual", auto-classified factType, documentIds from the selected element IDs, isSelected true, context "Manually added by user".

* The fact is appended to the active session’s detectedFacts array.

* The session phase transitions to "curating".

* The floating toolbar dismisses (textSelection or tableCellSelection is cleared).

 

h3. AC7: Persistent Mode

* After adding a fact, the add-fact mode remains active (isAddingManualFact stays true).

* The user can immediately select more content and add more facts without re-clicking "+ Add Fact".

* The purple instruction banner remains visible.

column1: Activate Manual Fact Addition Mode
column29:
As a tagging user, I want to activate a manual fact addition mode from the AI tagging fact list, so that I can select content in the document to add as facts that the AI missed.

 

Description: When viewing detected facts in an active AI tagging session, the user clicks "+ Add Fact" to enter a mode where document selections are captured as manual facts instead of triggering the normal tagging actions.
column363:
h3. AC1: Add Fact Button Visibility

* The "+ Add Fact" button appears in the fact list toolbar, to the right of the "N selected" count.

* The button is only visible when the session is in "facts_ready" or "curating" phase.

* The button is not visible when the session is in prediction, review, or resolved phases.

 

h3. AC2: Mode Activation

* Clicking "+ Add Fact" sets isAddingManualFact to true (global state).

* The button text changes to "× Cancel" with purple background/border styling.

* A purple instruction banner appears below the toolbar bar: "Select content in the document, then click Add to Session in the floating toolbar."

 

h3. AC3: Mode Deactivation

* Clicking "× Cancel" sets isAddingManualFact to false.

* The banner disappears. The button reverts to "+ Add Fact" with gray styling.

* The document floating toolbar returns to its normal behavior (Mark as Fact, Suggest tag with AI, Detect Facts).

column1: Manual Fact Addition
column29:
As a tagging user, I want to manually add facts that the AI detection missed to an active AI tagging session, so that I can include all relevant content for AI tag prediction without starting a new detection run.

 

Business Context: AI fact detection identifies the majority of taggable content, but it cannot guarantee 100% recall. Users may notice values, percentages, or text blocks in the document that the AI did not detect. Rather than forcing the user to re-run detection on a wider range or manually tag these facts outside the AI workflow, this feature allows them to select missed content directly in the document and add it to the current session. The manually added facts then participate in the same prediction, review, and accept flow as AI-detected facts.

column1: Session Management
column29:
As a tagging user, I want to see all AI tagging sessions for the document, navigate between them, and have resolved sessions automatically clean up, so that I can track and manage AI tagging activity.

 The AI Tagging panel opens to a session list view showing all sessions with their phase, initiator, and timestamps. Users can drill into any session. Resolved sessions auto-remove. Stale sessions show warnings. Locked sessions show indicators.
column363:
h3. AC27: Session List View

* The AI Tagging panel opens to a list of all sessions for the document, ordered by most recent first.

* Each session card shows: label, phase badge (color-coded), initiator name, relative timestamp.

* Stale sessions show a red warning icon on the card.

* The header shows total session count.

* An empty state message is shown when no sessions exist: "No AI tagging sessions yet. Select content and click Detect Facts to get started."

 

h3. AC28: Session Detail Navigation

* Clicking a session card navigates to the session detail view (fact list or prediction review depending on phase).

* "< All sessions" breadcrumb at the top navigates back to the session list.

* The session label and phase badge are shown in the detail view header.

 

h3. AC29: Collaboration Lock Indicator

* Sessions in pre-prediction phases (detection_initiated through prediction_initiated) show an amber lock banner: "Locked to {userName} until predictions are ready."

* The lock banner disappears when the session transitions to predictions_ready.

 

h3. AC30: Staleness Warning

* Sessions where the underlying document content has changed since detection show a red banner: "Document content has changed since detection. Facts may be outdated. Re-detect recommended."

* Staleness is determined by comparing the stored content hash against the current content hash.

 

h3. AC31: Undo Banner

* Sessions with accepted tags show a blue banner: "{N} tag(s) applied to document" with an "Undo all" button.

* Clicking "Undo all" removes all tags created by the session, resets predictions to pending, and shows a success notification.

* The undo banner disappears after undo (acceptedTagDocumentIds becomes empty).

 

h3. AC32: Auto-Cleanup of Resolved Sessions

* When all predictions in a session are either accepted or rejected (phase: fully_resolved), the session is automatically removed from the list after a 3-second delay.

* If the user was viewing the resolved session, the panel navigates back to the session list.

* Sessions with any pending predictions are NOT auto-removed.

 

h3. AC33: Session Deletion

* Each session card in the list has a delete button (trash icon).

* Deleting a session removes it from the list and clears the active session if it was being viewed.

* Deletion is logged in the audit trail.

 

h3. AC34: Audit Trail

* Every AI tagging action is logged with actionType "AI Tagging", user identity, timestamp, and action-specific details.

* Logged actions: session created, facts detected, predictions received, prediction accepted (with element name and confidence), prediction rejected, prediction swapped, bulk accept, re-predict, session undone, session deleted.

* Audit log entries are visible in the existing Audit Log modal.

column1: Session Management
column29: The AI Tagging panel opens to a session list view showing all sessions with their phase, initiator, and timestamps. Users can drill into any session. Resolved sessions auto-remove. Stale sessions show warnings. Locked sessions show indicators.

column1: Prediction Review and Tag Application
column29: As a tagging user, I want to review AI predictions with full tag details, edit properties inline, accept or reject individual predictions, swap to alternatives, and bulk-accept by confidence level, so that I can efficiently apply accurate XBRL tags to the document.
column363:
h3. AC18: Confidence Tile Bar

* A persistent bar at the top shows colored tiles for High (≥80%), Medium (60–79%), and Low (<60%) confidence counts.

* Tiles are always visible — they do not disappear after interaction.

* Clicking a tile toggles filtering: active tile shows thick border + shadow, list filters to that band. Clicking again clears the filter.

* Only one confidence filter can be active at a time.

* A "Confirm All (N)" / "Confirm Filtered (N)" button appears next to the tiles, with count reflecting only the pending predictions in the active filter.

 

h3. AC19: Prediction Card — Pending State

* Each pending card shows: fact value (monospace), element label (bold), element name (monospace, truncated), confidence badge (color-coded).

* Property pills row: period (sky), unit (emerald), scale (amber), sign (gray), decimals (gray). Clickable to open the inline editor.

* Dimension pills (violet) with axis=member format and individual confidence badges.

* "Edit properties" and "Reasoning" collapsible toggles.

* "Swap ▾", "Reject", "Accept" action buttons.

 

h3. AC20: Prediction Card — Accepted State

* Accepted cards show a compact green row with checkmark icon, fact value, element label, and "Accepted" badge.

* No action buttons are shown on accepted cards.

 

h3. AC21: Prediction Card — Rejected State

* Rejected cards show a compact dimmed row with X icon, strikethrough fact value, element label, and "Rejected" badge.

* No action buttons are shown on rejected cards.

 

h3. AC22: Inline Property Editing

* Expanding "Edit properties" shows dropdown selects for Period, Unit, Scale, Sign, and a text input for Decimals.

* Dropdowns are populated from the XBRL profile’s available periods, currencies, and scales.

* Changing any value immediately updates the prediction and marks it wasModifiedBeforeAccept: true.

* Modified predictions show an "edited" badge on the pills row and a "Modified" indicator.

* The inline editor uses an amber-bordered panel visually distinct from the Properties panel.

 

h3. AC23: Accept Creates Real XBRL Tag

* When Accept is clicked, the system calls handleBulkUpdate with the predicted element, period, unit, scale, sign, and members.

* A Tag entry is created in the document’s tag array with targetIds matching the fact’s documentIds.

* FactDetails are created/updated with the predicted attributes and isAiSuggested: true.

* The document element shows the standard XBRL tag visual indicator.

* The accepted documentIds are tracked in acceptedTagDocumentIds for undo.

 

h3. AC24: Swap to Alternative

* Clicking "Swap ▾" shows a dropdown with alternative suggestions ranked by confidence.

* Each alternative shows: element label, element name (mono), confidence badge, reason text.

* Selecting an alternative replaces the primary element. The old primary moves to the alternatives list.

* The prediction is marked wasModifiedBeforeAccept: true.

 

h3. AC25: Bulk Accept

* When no confidence filter is active, "Confirm All (N)" accepts all pending predictions.

* When a confidence filter is active, "Confirm Filtered (N)" accepts only the pending predictions matching the active confidence band.

* Each accepted prediction creates a real XBRL tag on the document.

* The count shown on the button reflects only pending predictions in the active filter, not total pending.

 

h3. AC26: Re-Prediction After Rejection

* When rejected predictions exist, a "Re-predict (N)" button appears in the footer.

* Clicking re-predict sends the rejected facts back to the prediction engine with an exclusion map of previously rejected elements.

* New predictions appear replacing the rejected ones, with different element suggestions.

* Previously rejected element names are never repeated for the same fact within the same session.

column1: Prediction Review and Tag Application
column29: After prediction, the side pane displays a persistent confidence tile bar for summary and filtering, followed by individual prediction cards. Each card shows the predicted tag signature and supports inline editing, accept, reject, and swap actions. Accepted predictions create real XBRL tags on the document.

column1: AI Tag Prediction
column29:
As a tagging user, I want the system to predict XBRL tags with full attribute sets and confidence scores for my curated facts, so that I can review AI suggestions before applying them to the document.

 

Description: When the user clicks "Predict Tags", the system sends the selected facts to the AI prediction engine along with the XBRL profile context. The engine returns predicted element names, dimension-member pairs, period, unit, scale, sign, decimals, confidence scores, reasoning narratives, and alternative suggestions. The session transitions to the prediction review view.
column363:
h3. AC14: Prediction Initiation

* Clicking "Predict Tags →" transitions the session to "prediction_initiated" phase.

* A progress bar animates during prediction.

* Only selected, non-already-tagged facts are sent for prediction.

 

h3. AC15: Prediction Request Payload

* The request includes: fact ID, value, context, factType, sourceType for each fact.

* The request includes XBRL profile metadata: taxonomy, taxonomy version, regulation, form type, period end date, available periods, available currencies/units, available scales.

* If re-predicting after rejections, the request includes an exclusion map of previously rejected element names per factId.

 

h3. AC16: Prediction Response

* Each prediction returns: elementName, elementLabel, confidence (0–100), reasoning narrative, predicted dimensions (axis/member pairs with individual confidence), period ID, unit, scale, sign (+/-), decimals, and up to N alternative element suggestions.

* All predictions start with status "pending".

* On completion, session transitions to "predictions_ready" (Review Needed badge).

* The collaboration lock releases — other users can now interact with the session.

 

h3. AC17: Prediction Context Handling

* For table facts, context includes the row label and column header.

* For narrative facts, context includes surrounding text (40 characters before and after the value).

* The prediction engine uses context to differentiate between ambiguous values (e.g., "5%" as revenue growth vs. tax rate).

column1: AI Tag Prediction
column29: When the user clicks "Predict Tags", the system sends the selected facts to the AI prediction engine along with the XBRL profile context. The engine returns predicted element names, dimension-member pairs, period, unit, scale, sign, decimals, confidence scores, reasoning narratives, and alternative suggestions. The session transitions to the prediction review view.

column1: Fact Curation and Side Pane Functions
column29:
As a tagging user, I want to curate detected facts by selecting or deselecting them, filtering by type, and visually connecting them to the document, so that I send only relevant facts for AI tag prediction.

 

Description: After detection, the side pane displays all detected facts with checkboxes, type/source badges, and clustering. The user can toggle individual facts, use Select All / Deselect All, filter by type and source, and click facts to highlight them in the document. Selected facts show persistent marks on the document.
column363:
h3. AC8: Fact Selection Checkboxes

* Each non-already-tagged fact has a checkbox, defaulting to selected (checked).

* Toggling a checkbox includes or excludes the fact from prediction.

* The session phase transitions to "Curating" when any checkbox is toggled.

* The selected fact count is displayed next to the "Predict Tags →" button.

 

h3. AC9: Select All / Deselect All

* "Select all" selects all non-already-tagged facts.

* "Deselect all" deselects all facts.

* Button label toggles between "Select all" and "Deselect all" based on current state.

 

h3. AC10: Fact Type and Source Filtering

* A filter bar provides dropdown filters for fact type (All types, Monetary, Percentage, Text Block, etc.) and source type (All sources, Table, Narrative).

* Applying a filter shows only matching facts in the list. Clusters containing no matching children are hidden.

* The filter bar shows the total fact count.

 

h3. AC11: Persistent Document Marks

* When a fact’s checkbox is selected, the corresponding document element(s) receive a persistent teal left border and light teal background.

* When a fact’s checkbox is deselected, the persistent mark is removed.

* Marks are cleared when the session is closed or the user navigates away.

* Multiple selected facts show multiple marks simultaneously in the document.

 

h3. AC12: Click-to-Highlight Navigation

* Clicking a fact row (not the checkbox) highlights the corresponding document element with a prominent teal ring and glow shadow.

* The document scrolls to bring the highlighted element into view.

* The highlight fades after 1.5 seconds.

* The AI Tagging panel remains open — no switch to Properties panel.

 

h3. AC13: Predict Tags Button

* The "Predict Tags →" button appears at the bottom of the fact list.

* The button shows the count of selected facts: "N facts ready".

* The button is disabled when no facts are selected or when prediction is in progress.

* Clicking initiates the prediction flow (Next EPIC).

column1: Results List
column29:
As a *document editor user*

I want to *see all search matches in a scrollable list grouped by document section*

So that *I can get an overview of where a term appears and jump to specific occurrences*
column363:
* *AC10.1* Search results are displayed in a scrollable list below the options/scope controls.

* *AC10.2* Results are grouped by content block (paragraph, table, or image) with a sticky section header.

* *AC10.3* Each section header shows the block type icon, a text preview of the block, and the match count for that block.

* *AC10.4* Each result row shows a sequential match number, a context snippet (24 chars before and after the match), and the matched text highlighted.

* *AC10.5* Table matches include a badge showing the row and column number (e.g. 'Row 2, Col 1').

* *AC10.6* Image matches include a badge showing the field name ('Alt text' or 'Caption').

* *AC10.7* The active match row is visually highlighted and automatically scrolls into view within the list.

* *AC10.8* When there are no matches, an empty state message is shown: 'No matches found'.

* *AC10.9* Before any search term is entered, the empty state shows: 'Type to search the document'.

column1: Special Characters
column29:
As a *document editor user*

I want to *search for and replace special characters like paragraph marks, dashes, and non-breaking spaces using shorthand codes*

So that *I can clean up imported or pasted content that contains invisible or non-standard characters*
column363:
* *AC9.1* The following 13 special character codes are available in both Find and Replace fields: ^p (paragraph mark), ^t (tab), ^l (manual line break), ^s (nonbreaking space), ^~ (nonbreaking hyphen), ^- (optional hyphen), ^+ (em dash), ^= (en dash), ^m (manual page break), ^14 (column break), ^6 (section character §), ^% (paragraph character ¶), ^^ (caret literal).

* *AC9.2* The ^& (Find What Text) code is available in the Replace field only and inserts the verbatim matched text at that position.

* *AC9.3* Clicking a special character code in the Options dropdown inserts the code at the cursor position in the last-focused input (Find or Replace).

* *AC9.4* The ^& code is NOT shown in the Special Characters list when the Find input was last focused.

* *AC9.5* Special character codes are expanded correctly at search time in literal mode. They are NOT expanded in regex mode.

* *AC9.6* The Special Characters section header dynamically labels the target field: 'Insert into find field' or 'Insert into replace field'.

column1: Regular Expression Search
column29:
As a *power user* 

I want to *search using JavaScript regular expression patterns*

So that *I can find complex patterns like date formats, numeric ranges, or repeated terms in one search*
column363:
* *AC8.1* When Use regular expression is on, the Find input accepts and evaluates JavaScript regex syntax.

* *AC8.2* If the regex pattern is syntactically invalid, no matches are returned and a red error message is shown below the Options button describing the error.

* *AC8.3* Capture group back-references ($1, $2, $&) in the Replace field are correctly resolved in regex mode.

* *AC8.4* Whole word, Match prefix, and Match suffix are all disabled when regex mode is active.

* *AC8.5* Special character expansion (^p, ^t, etc.) is NOT applied in regex mode — the pattern is used verbatim.

* *AC8.6* Toggling regex mode off restores any previously active Whole word / prefix / suffix settings.

column1: Fact Curation and Side Pane Functions
column29: After detection, the side pane displays all detected facts with checkboxes, type/source badges, and clustering. The user can toggle individual facts, use Select All / Deselect All, filter by type and source, and click facts to highlight them in the document. Selected facts show persistent marks on the document.

column1: Match Prefix and Match Suffix
column29:
As a *financial document editor user*

I want to *restrict matches to text that appears at the start or end of a word*

So that *I can find 'pre' as a prefix (matching 'preview', 'prepare') without matching 'represent'*
column363:
* *AC7.1* When Match prefix is on, the search term only matches when it appears at the START of a word.

* *AC7.2* When Match suffix is on, the search term only matches when it appears at the END of a word.

* *AC7.3* When both Match prefix and Match suffix are on simultaneously, only standalone whole-word matches are returned (equivalent to Whole word).

* *AC7.4* Match prefix and Match suffix are disabled and greyed out when Whole word is active.

* *AC7.5* Match prefix and Match suffix are disabled and greyed out when Use regular expression is active.

* *AC7.6* A hint text 'Unavailable when Whole word is on' or 'Unavailable in regex mode' is shown below the disabled checkboxes.

* *AC7.7* Toggling Match prefix or Match suffix while a search is active immediately re-runs the search.

column1: Match Case & Whole Word Matching
column29:
As a *document editor user*

I want to *search with case sensitivity enabled*

So that *I can distinguish between 'Total' and 'total' in financial terminology*

Also, I want to *restrict search matches to whole words only*

So that *Searching 'ion' does not match 'validation', 'section', or 'discretion'*
column363:
h1. Match Case

* *AC5.1* When Match case is off (default), 'total' matches 'Total', 'TOTAL', and 'total'.
* *AC5.2* When Match case is on, 'total' matches only 'total' — not 'Total' or 'TOTAL'.
* *AC5.3* Toggling Match case while a search is active immediately re-runs the search and updates results

h1. Whole Word Matching

* *AC6.1* When Whole word is off (default), 'ion' matches inside 'validation' and 'section'.

* *AC6.2* When Whole word is on, 'ion' only matches the standalone word 'ion'.

* *AC6.3* Whole word is disabled and greyed out when Use regular expression is active.
* *AC6.4* Toggling Whole word while a search is active immediately re-runs the search.

column1: Content Selection and Fact Detection
column29:
As a tagging user, I want to select content in the document (paragraphs or table cells) and invoke AI-driven fact detection, so that the system identifies taggable facts within my selected range.

 

The user selects content in the document editor and clicks "Detect Facts" in the floating toolbar. The system analyzes the selected content, identifies taggable facts (monetary values, percentages, text blocks), classifies each by type and source, and presents them in the AI Tagging side pane. A new session is created to track this detection run.
column363:
h3. AC1: Narrative Text Selection

* When user selects text by click-and-drag in a narrative paragraph, a floating toolbar appears below the selection with a "Detect Facts" button.

* The toolbar also shows "Mark as Fact" and "Suggest tag with AI" buttons.

* The floating toolbar appears immediately at the selection endpoint.

* When no content is selected, no floating toolbar appears.

 

h3. AC2: Table Cell Selection — Single Cell

* When user clicks a single table cell, the "Detect Facts" floating toolbar appears immediately below the cell on the first click.

* The Properties panel does NOT open or override the toolbar.

* The panel override lock is activated during table cell selection and released when clicking outside the table.

 

h3. AC3: Table Cell Selection — Multi-Cell Drag

* When user drags across multiple table cells, all selected cells are highlighted.

* The "Detect Facts" toolbar appears below the selection and reflects all selected cell IDs.

* The Properties panel does NOT open during drag selection.

 

h3. AC4: Session Creation

* Clicking "Detect Facts" creates a new AI tagging session with a unique ID and timestamp.

* The session label reflects the content type: "Narrative Selection", "Table Selection", or "Mixed Selection".

* The session records: initiator user identity, content hash, document version, XBRL profile reference.

* The AI Tagging panel opens in the right sidebar.

* The session appears at the top of the session list.

 

h3. AC5: Detection Progress

* During detection, a progress bar animates in the session detail view.

* The session phase badge shows "Detecting" (green).

* Upon completion, the phase transitions to "Facts Ready" (blue).

 

h3. AC6: Fact Detection Results

* Each detected fact shows: value, context snippet, fact type badge (Monetary, %, Text Block, Shares, Per Share), and source type badge (Table, Narrative).

* For table content, each detected monetary/percentage value maps to its specific cell ID in the document.

* For narrative content, individual monetary/percentage facts map to the specific word span containing the value. Text block facts map to ALL word spans in the selection.

* Facts in content that already has XBRL tags are shown with "Already tagged" badge and greyed out — not selectable.

* If no taggable facts are detected, the user sees an informational message and the session is not persisted.

 

h3. AC7: Fact Clustering

* Overlapping facts within the same text span are grouped into expandable clusters.

* Cluster rows show the parent text span, a "Cluster · N" badge, and an expand/collapse arrow.

* Expanding a cluster reveals child facts, each with individual checkboxes, type badges, and source badges.

* Clusters default to collapsed state.

column1: Search Scope Control
column29:
As a *document editor user*

I want to *restrict search to specific content types or a selected portion of the document*

So that *I can focus search results on the section I'm working on without noise from other content*
column363:
* *AC4.1* The scope dropdown offers four options: All, Paragraphs, Tables, Images.

* *AC4.2* Selecting Paragraphs restricts search to paragraph text blocks only.

* *AC4.3* Selecting Tables restricts search to table cell values across all rows and columns.

* *AC4.4* Selecting Images restricts search to image alt text and caption fields only.

* *AC4.5* When text is selected in the editor before pressing Ctrl+F, the 'In selection' button is automatically activated.

* *AC4.6* The 'In selection' button is shown as active (blue) when the scope is pinned to selected blocks.

* *AC4.7* A blue banner below the scope row confirms 'Searching in N blocks only' when in-selection scope is active.

* *AC4.8* Clicking the active 'In selection' button deactivates it and returns search scope to 'All'.

* *AC4.9* The 'In selection' button is disabled (greyed out) when no text is selected and no selection scope is active.
* *AC4.10* Closing the search panel clears the selection scope. The scope resets to 'All' on next open.

column1: Find & Replace
column29:
As a *document editor user*

I want to *replace individual or all occurrences of matched text*

So that *I can efficiently correct terminology, labels, or values across the document*
column363:
* *AC3.1* Pressing Ctrl+H opens the Search tab in Find & Replace mode with focus in the Replace input.

* *AC3.2* The Find & Replace toggle button switches the panel between Find and Find & Replace modes.

* *AC3.3* The Replace and Replace All buttons are disabled when there are no matches.

* *AC3.4* Clicking Replace replaces the currently active match and advances to the next match.

* *AC3.5* After the last match is replaced, the match counter shows '0' and buttons disable.

* *AC3.6* Clicking Replace All replaces all matches in the current scope in one operation.

* *AC3.7* A toast notification appears after Replace All confirming the number of replacements made (e.g. '14 replacements made').

* *AC3.8* Replace operations are reversible via Undo (Ctrl+Z).
* *AC3.9* Replacing a match with an empty string (blank Replace field) deletes the matched text.

column1: Match Navigation
column29:
As a *document editor user*

I want to *navigate between search matches using keyboard and mouse controls*

So that *I can move through results efficiently without using a mouse exclusively*
column363:
* *AC2.1* Pressing Enter or clicking the Down chevron advances to the next match.

* *AC2.2* Pressing Shift+Enter or clicking the Up chevron goes to the previous match.

* *AC2.3* Pressing F3 advances to the next match; Shift+F3 goes to the previous match.

* *AC2.4* Navigation wraps around — going past the last match returns to the first, and vice versa.

* *AC2.5* Navigation buttons are disabled (greyed out) when there are no matches.

* *AC2.6* The active match highlight changes visually from other match highlights to indicate the current position.

* *AC2.7* The document scrolls to bring the active match into view when navigating.
* *AC2.8* Clicking a result row in the results list jumps directly to that match and sets it as active.

column1: Content Selection and Fact Detection
column29: The user selects content in the document editor and clicks "Detect Facts" in the floating toolbar. The system analyzes the selected content, identifies taggable facts (monetary values, percentages, text blocks), classifies each by type and source, and presents them in the AI Tagging side pane. A new session is created to track this detection run.

column1: Basic Find
column29:
As a *document editor user*

I want to *search for text within my document using a search panel*

So that *I can quickly locate specific content without scrolling manually*
column363:
* *AC1.1* Pressing Ctrl+F opens the Search tab with focus in the Find input.

* *AC1.2* Typing in the Find input triggers a search with a 200ms debounce — no immediate search on each keystroke.

* *AC1.3* All matching text in the document is highlighted with a yellow overlay.

* *AC1.4* A match counter badge inside the Find input shows 'current/total' (e.g. '1/14').

* *AC1.5* The badge displays '0' in red when no matches are found.

* *AC1.6* Pressing Escape or clicking X closes the panel and clears all highlights.

* *AC1.7* Clearing the Find input immediately clears all highlights and resets the counter.

column1: Find & Replace — Document Editor
column29:
Users need the ability to search for and replace text across all content types in an XBRL financial document — paragraphs, tables, and images — with support for advanced matching options, special character handling, and scoped search.

The feature is accessed via Ctrl+F (Find mode) and Ctrl+H (Find & Replace mode) and operates entirely within the left sidebar Search tab.
column372: Implement a full-featured Find & Replace capability within the Rainbow 5.0 XBRL document editor, surfaced as a dedicated Search tab in the left sidebar panel.

column1: Text color
column363:
h1. SECTION 1 — CLARIFICATIONS NEEDED

The following ambiguities must be resolved. Acceptance Criteria assume *Microsoft Word Desktop default behavior*.

# *Color Palette Scope*
#* Confirm whether the Editor supports:
#** Theme colors
#** Standard colors
#** Custom RGB/HEX colors
#* AC assumes *theme + standard palette*, with custom color optional.
# *Automatic Color*
#* Confirm whether “Automatic” text color exists and maps to Word’s default black.
# *Text Color vs Highlight*
#* Confirm text color is independent from text highlight (background color).
# *Partial Character Coloring*
#* Confirm coloring supports character‑level selection within words.
# *Hyperlink Color Rules*
#* Confirm whether hyperlink text color overrides manual color, following Word rules.
# *Nested Tables*
#* Confirm whether nested tables are supported. AC assumes *top‑level tables only*.
# *Track Changes*
#* Confirm Track Changes is out of scope. AC assumes *disabled*.

----

h1. SECTION 2 — FEATURE SUMMARY

*Text Color* allows users to change the foreground color of selected text characters.

The Editor must match *Microsoft Word Desktop* behavior across:

* Manual application
* Uploaded documents
* Pasted content

Text color must:

* Apply at character level
* Preserve existing formatting (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough)
* Persist through undo/redo
* Sync in real time across collaborators
* Survive export and re‑import without degradation

----

h1. SECTION 3 — ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

{quote}Only *BLOCKER, CRITICAL, and MAJOR* issues are defined.{quote}

----

h2. 1. Happy Path — Manual Entry (Outside Table)

*AC‑TC‑HP‑01 (BLOCKER)*
*GIVEN* plain text exists outside any table
*WHEN* the user selects text and chooses a color from the *Text Color dropdown* in the Editor toolbar
*THEN* the selected text changes to the chosen color exactly as it would in Microsoft Word Desktop

*TEST HINT:*
Apply the same color in Word and visually compare RGB appearance.

----

h2. 2. Happy Path — Manual Entry (Inside Table, Top‑Level)

*AC‑TC‑HP‑02 (BLOCKER)*
*GIVEN* the cursor is inside a *top‑level table cell*
*WHEN* the user applies a text color
*THEN* only the selected text inside the cell changes color and table layout remains unchanged, matching Word

*TEST HINT:*
Verify no row height or cell spacing change.

----

h2. 3. Upload — DOCX (Outside Table)

*AC‑TC‑UP‑01 (CRITICAL)*
*GIVEN* a {{.docx}} file created in Word contains colored text outside a table
*WHEN* the document is uploaded into the Editor
*THEN* all text colors are preserved per character exactly as displayed in Word

*TEST HINT:*
Check multiple colors across different paragraphs.

----

h2. 4. Upload — DOCX (Inside Table, Top‑Level)

*AC‑TC‑UP‑02 (CRITICAL)*
*GIVEN* a {{.docx}} file contains colored text inside a top‑level table cell
*WHEN* uploaded into the Editor
*THEN* all colors are preserved with no conversion to default color

*TEST HINT:*
Verify mixed colors within the same cell.

----

h2. 5. Copy‑Paste — From Word (Outside Table)

*AC‑TC‑CP‑01 (CRITICAL)*
*GIVEN* colored text is copied from Word outside a table
*WHEN* pasted into the Editor
*THEN* text colors are retained exactly as in Word

*TEST HINT:*
Paste using Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V without special paste.

----

h2. 6. Copy‑Paste — From Word (Inside Table)

*AC‑TC‑CP‑02 (CRITICAL)*
*GIVEN* colored text is copied from a Word table cell
*WHEN* pasted into an Editor table cell
*THEN* text color and table structure are preserved as in Word

*TEST HINT:*
Confirm no fallback to black or theme default.

----

h2. 7. Keyboard & Accessibility

*AC‑TC‑KA‑01 (MAJOR)*
*GIVEN* text is selected
*WHEN* the user opens the *Text Color dropdown* using keyboard navigation
*THEN* a color can be selected and applied without mouse interaction, matching Word accessibility behavior

*TEST HINT:*
Navigate using Tab, Arrow keys, and Enter.

----

h2. 8. UI State Synchronization

*AC‑TC‑UI‑01 (MAJOR)*
*GIVEN* selected text has a specific color
*WHEN* the cursor selection is active
*THEN* the *Text Color toolbar icon* displays the correct active color, matching Word

*TEST HINT:*
Move cursor across text with different colors.

----

h2. 9. Negative — No Selection

*AC‑TC‑NEG‑01 (MAJOR)*
*GIVEN* no text is selected
*WHEN* the user changes the Text Color
*THEN* no existing text is modified and newly typed text follows Word behavior

*TEST HINT:*
Type new text after color selection.

----

h2. 10. Boundary — Multiple Colors Selection

*AC‑TC‑BD‑01 (MAJOR)*
*GIVEN* selected text contains multiple colors
*WHEN* the user applies a new text color
*THEN* all selected characters change to the new color exactly as Word does

*TEST HINT:*
Select rainbow‑colored text and apply one color.

----

h2. 11. Undo / Redo

*AC‑TC‑UR‑01 (BLOCKER)*
*GIVEN* text color is applied
*WHEN* the user presses *Ctrl + Z*
*THEN* original text color is fully restored

*AND WHEN* *Ctrl + Y* is pressed
*THEN* the new text color is reapplied exactly

*TEST HINT:*
Perform repeated undo/redo cycles.

----

h2. 12. Collaboration

*AC‑TC‑COL‑01 (BLOCKER)*
*GIVEN* two users are editing the same document
*WHEN* User A changes text color
*THEN* User B sees the change in real time and identical to Word behavior

*TEST HINT:*
Apply rapid successive color changes.

----

h2. 13. Integration — Export

*AC‑TC‑INT‑01 (CRITICAL)*
*GIVEN* the document contains colored text
*WHEN* exported to {{.docx}}
*THEN* all text colors appear correctly when opened in Word Desktop

*TEST HINT:*
Open exported file and compare color palette values.

----

h1. SECTION 4 — TEST CASE MATRIX

||Populate Method||Outside Table||Inside Table (Top‑Level)||
|Manual Entry|✅ AC‑TC‑HP‑01|✅ AC‑TC‑HP‑02|
|Upload (.docx)|✅ AC‑TC‑UP‑01|✅ AC‑TC‑UP‑02|
|Copy‑Paste (Word)|✅ AC‑TC‑CP‑01|✅ AC‑TC‑CP‑02|

----

h1. SECTION 5 — OUT OF SCOPE

* Track Changes color semantics
* Text highlight (background color)
* Gradient or patterned text
* Nested tables
* Mobile or touch input
* PDF export color fidelity
* Theme re‑mapping across templates

----

h1. SECTION 6 — WORD DEVIATION LOG

||Deviation||Severity||Notes||
|Colors mapped to nearest theme color|CRITICAL|Word preserves exact RGB|
|Color lost during paste in tables|CRITICAL|Word retains formatting|
|Toolbar does not reflect active color|MAJOR|Word updates instantly|
|Undo merges color with text edits|BLOCKER|Word treats color as atomic|

column1: Underline
column363:
h1. SECTION 1 — CLARIFICATIONS NEEDED

The following ambiguities must be confirmed before final execution. Acceptance Criteria below assume *Microsoft Word Desktop default behavior*.

# *Underline Style*
#* Confirm whether only _single underline_ is supported or if _double underline_ must also be supported.
#* AC assumes *single underline only*.
# *Partial Character Selection*
#* Confirm whether underlining part of a word behaves character‑level, matching Word.
# *Underline with Existing Formatting*
#* Confirm underline must preserve bold, italic, strikethrough, font size, color, and background highlight.
# *Underline in Hyperlinks*
#* Confirm whether hyperlink underline rules follow Word defaults.
# *Nested Tables*
#* Confirm whether nested tables are supported. AC assumes *top‑level tables only*.
# *Track Changes*
#* Confirm Track Changes is out of scope. AC assumes *disabled*.
# *HTML* {{<u>}} *vs* {{<span style>}} *Priority*
#* Confirm correct precedence during HTML upload/paste. AC assumes *visual parity with Word*.

----

h1. SECTION 2 — FEATURE SUMMARY

*Underline* visually emphasizes text by placing a continuous line beneath characters.

The Editor must match *Microsoft Word Desktop* behavior across:

* Manual application
* Uploaded documents
* Pasted content

Underline must:

* Be non‑destructive
* Apply at character level
* Persist through undo/redo
* Synchronize in real time
* Export and re‑import without loss

----

h1. SECTION 3 — ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

{quote}Only *BLOCKER, CRITICAL, and MAJOR* issues are covered.{quote}

----

h2. 1. Happy Path — Manual Entry (Outside Table)

*AC‑UL‑HP‑01 (BLOCKER)*
*GIVEN* plain text exists outside any table
*WHEN* the user selects text and clicks the *Underline button* in the Editor toolbar
*THEN* the selected text is underlined exactly as rendered in Microsoft Word Desktop

*TEST HINT:*
Use identical font and size in Word and visually compare underline thickness and position.

----

h2. 2. Happy Path — Manual Entry (Inside Table, Top‑Level)

*AC‑UL‑HP‑02 (BLOCKER)*
*GIVEN* the cursor is inside a *top‑level table cell*
*WHEN* the user selects text and applies Underline
*THEN* only the selected text inside the cell is underlined with no change to row height or cell padding, matching Word

*TEST HINT:*
Verify no table reflow occurs.

----

h2. 3. Upload — DOCX (Outside Table)

*AC‑UL‑UP‑01 (CRITICAL)*
*GIVEN* a {{.docx}} file created in Word contains underlined text outside a table
*WHEN* the document is uploaded into the Editor
*THEN* all underline formatting is preserved exactly as displayed in Word

*TEST HINT:*
Compare underlined character count before and after upload.

----

h1. SECTION 1 — CLARIFICATIONS NEEDED

The following gaps must be confirmed before final test execution. Acceptance Criteria below assume *Microsoft Word Desktop (Microsoft 365, Windows 11)* default behavior unless stated.

# *Partial Selection Rule*
#* When only part of a word is selected and strikethrough is applied, confirm whether the Editor must mirror Word by striking only the selected characters.
# *Mixed Formatting Rule*
#* Confirm whether applying strikethrough preserves existing formatting (bold, italic, underline, font size, color) exactly as Word does.
# *Nested Table Support*
#* Confirm whether nested tables (table inside table cell) are supported in the Editor and must behave identically to top-level tables.
# *Track Changes*
#* Confirm that Track Changes is out of scope. AC assumes Track Changes is NOT enabled.
# *Mobile / Touch Input*
#* Confirm desktop-only scope. AC assumes keyboard and mouse input only.
# *Paste Source Priority*
#* When pasting from Word containing both {{<s>}} and {{<del>}} styles, confirm which takes priority. AC assumes visual rendering parity with Word.

----

h1. SECTION 2 — FEATURE SUMMARY

*Strikethrough* allows users to visually mark text content with a horizontal line through the text.

The Editor must match *Microsoft Word Desktop* behavior across:

* Manual application
* Imported content
* Pasted content

The feature must work:

* Inside and outside tables
* In collaborative editing
* With undo/redo
* Via UI, keyboard, and accessibility tools

Strikethrough must be:

* Non-destructive
* Persisted in document state
* Export-safe
* Real-time synchronized

column363:
h2. SECTION 1 — CLARIFICATIONS NEEDED

No clarifications needed.

* Italic behavior is clearly defined in Microsoft Word.
* Behavior is consistent across all populate methods.
* Behavior is consistent inside and outside tables, including nested tables.

----

h2. SECTION 2 — FEATURE SUMMARY

The Italic feature allows users to apply or remove italic formatting to text using the Italic toolbar button or the Ctrl+I keyboard shortcut.
The feature applies to text entered manually, uploaded from HTML or Word documents, or pasted from HTML or Word sources.
Italic formatting must behave consistently for content inside table cells and outside tables, including top‑level and nested tables.
Microsoft Word (Desktop, Microsoft 365, Windows 11) is the baseline for formatting appearance, interaction, undo behavior, and collaboration updates.
No deviations from Word behavior are defined for this feature.

* *Populate Method:* Manual Entry
* *Content Context:* Both (outside table, inside top‑level and nested table cells)

*GIVEN* the cursor is placed within unformatted text
*WHEN* the user clicks the *Italic button* in the formatting toolbar
*THEN* the selected text renders with italic font‑style, matching Microsoft Word italic rendering.

[TEST HINT] validation: inspect rendered text and confirm font‑style is italic

----

* *Populate Method:* All methods
* *Content Context:* Both

[TEST HINT] validation: type text after enabling Italic and confirm font‑style

----

h3. 3.3 Boundary Conditions

h4. ITALIC‑AC‑004 — Single Character Formatting

* *Populate Method:* All methods
* *Content Context:* Both

*GIVEN* a single character is selected

*THEN* only the selected character is italicized, with adjacent characters unaffected.

[TEST HINT] validation: compare font‑style of selected vs surrounding characters

* *Populate Method:* Upload Word, Paste Word

[TEST HINT] validation: inspect accessibility tree and ARIA attributes

h3. 3.6 Integration with Other Editor Features

*THEN* the italic change is recorded as a formatting change, matching Microsoft Word behavior.

[TEST HINT] validation: verify tracked formatting change indicator

----

h3. 3.7 Undo / Redo

h4. ITALIC‑AC‑009 — Undo Italic Formatting

* *Populate Method:* All methods
* *Content Context:* Both

*GIVEN* italic formatting has been applied
*WHEN* the user presses *Ctrl+Z* once
*THEN* italic formatting is fully removed, restoring the prior formatting state.

[TEST HINT] validation: confirm font‑style returns to non‑italic

* *Content Context:* Both

*THEN* User B sees the italic formatting applied in real time, matching Microsoft Word co‑authoring behavior.

column1: Approval, audit trail, and history work across the module
column29: As a user, I want approval and history capabilities to persist across the XBRL module so that changes are traceable and review decisions are supported over time.
column363:
h3. Acceptance Criteria

# The module supports approving facts.
# The module records audit log entries when fact data changes.
# The module records fact history over time.
# The module supports restoring fact history snapshots.
# History and audit behavior are not restricted to one single mode, even though they are especially important in Tagging mode and Review mode.
# When a fact is edited in Tagging mode, the resulting changes are reflected in the audit trail and history.
# Review-oriented users can inspect history when validating prior changes.
# Approval logic can block progress when unresolved errors or warnings remain, as described in the validation behavior.
# Approval and history remain traceable to the selected fact so users can understand what changed, when it changed, and in what review context decisions were made.
# The UI supports history visibility through the right-side pane or equivalent detail surface.
# The module preserves the relationship between fact data, validation state, and history records instead of treating them as unrelated features.
# The workflow supports future review-mode maturity where approval and history become especially significant for formal review processes.

column1: VIP taxonomy | EX 99r | iXBRL output generation
column29:
*iXBRL Output Generation Specification*

# *Document Structure*

The generated output shall be a valid iXBRL HTML document containing the required HTML structure and embedded XBRL structure.

The output shall include:

* HTML root element with required namespace declarations
* HTML head section
* HTML body section
* iXBRL header
* references
* resources
* hidden facts, where applicable
* visible inline facts, where applicable

# *HTML Head*

The HTML head shall contain the document title and required metadata.

# *HTML Body*

The HTML body shall contain the visible exhibit content and the iXBRL structural components required for tagging.

# *iXBRL Header*

The iXBRL header shall include:

* hidden section
* references section
* resources section

# *References*

 

The references section shall contain the required taxonomy reference information such as schema references and related linkbase references, as applicable.

# *Resources*

The resources section shall contain the required XBRL resources such as contexts and units used by the facts in the document.

# *Hidden Facts*

The hidden section shall contain facts that are required in the XBRL output but are not intended for visible display.

# *Visible Inline Facts*

The visible content shall contain inline XBRL facts for numeric and non-numeric data, as applicable.

# *Fact Integrity*

All generated facts shall correctly reference the required context, unit, and taxonomy concept.

The generated output shall preserve consistency between the visible HTML content and the embedded XBRL data.

*10. Historic Exhibit Handling*

If an exhibit form is configured by Admin as *EX-99.4R HISTORIC*, then any use of that exhibit within a workspace shall be processed using *Historic altering logic*.

The generated output shall preserve the Historic classification and shall not be treated as standard EX-99.4R output.

For such Historic exhibits, the system shall handle the exhibit as Historic during output generation, including any applicable labeling, metadata, and rendering behavior.

*11. Structural Validity*

The generated output shall remain structurally valid iXBRL regardless of whether the exhibit is standard or Historic.

*12. Validation*

The system shall validate that all required iXBRL sections are present and that Historic handling is applied where the exhibit type is *EX-99.4R HISTORIC*.
column363:
h3. AC1. Historic exhibit identification

When an exhibit form has been configured by Admin as *EX-99.4R HISTORIC*, the system must recognize that exhibit as a Historic exhibit type whenever it is selected or used within a workspace. The Historic classification must remain associated with the exhibit throughout the output generation process.

h3. AC2. Application of Historic altering logic

For any workspace that includes an exhibit configured as *EX-99.4R HISTORIC*, the system must apply the defined Historic altering logic during iXBRL output generation. The exhibit must be processed through the Historic handling path and not through the standard EX-99.4R generation flow.

h3. AC3. Preservation of Historic classification in output

The generated output must preserve the Historic nature of the exhibit. Wherever the exhibit type, exhibit label, metadata, or rendering identifies the exhibit, it must continue to reflect that the exhibit is Historic.

h3. AC4. No standard EX-99.4R treatment

An exhibit configured as *EX-99.4R HISTORIC* must not be generated, labeled, or validated as a standard *EX-99.4R* exhibit. The system must clearly distinguish Historic exhibit processing from standard exhibit processing.

h3. AC5. Valid iXBRL output after Historic handling

The application of Historic altering logic must not break the iXBRL output structure. The generated document must remain a valid iXBRL HTML output with the required structural sections, references, resources, and fact relationships intact.

h3. AC6. Validation of Historic processing

The system must validate that Historic handling has been applied whenever the exhibit type is *EX-99.4R HISTORIC*. If the exhibit is processed as a standard EX-99.4R exhibit instead of as Historic, the output must be considered incorrect.

column1: Document-Level Image Management
column29: As a Document Author, I want to view, select, reorder, and manage all images through a centralized panel and supporting tools, so that I can efficiently work with multiple images and control their visibility, layering, and lifecycle.
column363:
h3. AC 5.1: Selection Pane — Opening

* Ribbon Arrange group: Selection Pane button. Also via sidebarTabChange event with panel: SelectionPane.

h3. AC 5.2: Selection Pane — Image List

* Images listed in reverse order (topmost layer first). Count header: Layers icon + “N images in document” + “Ordered by layer · top to bottom.”

* Each row: 40×28 px thumbnail, label (caption → altText → “Image N”), dimensions monospace, wrap mode, z-index badge if non-zero.

* Selected row: zinc-50 bg + 2 px dark left border. Click row: selects image in document.

* No images: empty state with Image icon + “No images” + “Insert an image to see it listed here.”

h3. AC 5.3: Visibility Toggle

* Eye/EyeOff button per row (hover-visible; always visible for selected row).

* Hidden: thumbnail dims (opacity 0.25), label strikethrough + muted, CSS visibility:hidden in document. Show: normal.

h3. AC 5.4: Selection Pane Layer Controls

* Selected image: 4 buttons at bottom — Bring to Front, Send to Back, Bring Forward, Send Backward. Hidden when no selection.

h3. AC 5.5: Sidebar Tab Navigation and Resize

* Two equal-width tabs: Selection (Layers icon) / Properties (Image icon). Bottom-border active indicator. X close button.

* Left-edge resize handle: 1 px wide, full height, opacity 0→1 on hover, zinc-400 bg, cursor col-resize. Min 280 px, max 600 px.

h3. AC 5.6: Context Menu

* Right-click image: menu at click position. Items: Alt Text (♿), Image Properties (⚙️), Replace Image (🔄), Copy Image (📋), Delete Image (🗑️ red).

* Alt Text: selects image. Properties: selects + opens sidebar Properties tab. Replace: opens dialog in Replace mode.

* Copy: duplicates after original (new ID + timestamp). “Image copied” toast. Delete: no confirmation. “Image deleted” toast.

* Click outside closes menu.

h3. AC 5.7: Keyboard Shortcuts

* Del/Backspace: delete (no confirm). Escape: deselect (or cancel crop).

* Ctrl+X: cut (copy to clipboard + delete). Ctrl+C: copy to in-memory clipboard. Ctrl+V: paste (new ID + timestamp, after selected image).

* Arrows: nudge 1 px (Shift: 10 px). Ctrl+Z: undo. Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z: redo.

* All suppressed in INPUT/TEXTAREA.

h3. AC 5.8: Toast Notifications

* Bottom-center, 3s auto-dismiss. Icons: success (CheckCircle emerald), error (AlertCircle red), info (Info zinc).

* Messages: Image inserted/replaced/deleted/copied/repositioned/cut, Brought forward/to front, Sent backward/to back.

* Single toast visible. New replaces existing.

h3. AC 5.9: Undo / Redo

* Ctrl+Z: undo last document change (insert, delete, property change, reposition). Ctrl+Y/Ctrl+Shift+Z: redo.

* Toolbar Undo/Redo buttons: disabled (reduced opacity, cursor not-allowed) when unavailable.

h3. AC 5.10: Find & Replace Integration

* F&R active + image alt/caption matches: floating badge top-left with search icon, count, location (“in alt text,” “in caption,” or “(alt: N, caption: N)”).

* Muted badge: yellow-100 bg. Active match badge: amber-400 bg + data-find-match-active for scroll-into-view.

* Images included/excluded via searchScope (“images” or “all”).

h3. AC 5.11: Image Error Fallback

* Image load failure (broken src, network error): onError replaces src with grey placeholder SVG (200×120 px, “Image not available”).

* Display-only substitution — stored src unchanged. Valid src on re-render shows correct image.

h3. AC 5.12: Image Rendering Pipeline

* CSS filter: brightness(%), contrast(%), saturate(%), blur(px for sharpness). All defaults: filter none.

* CSS border: {width}px {dashStyle} \{color}. Applied to img style.

* CSS transform: translate(nudgeX, nudgeY) rotate(deg) scaleX(-1 if flipH) scaleY(-1 if flipV). Applied to figure.

* Crop: wrapper div sized to visible %, img offset by negative crop amounts, overflow hidden.
* Opacity: img opacity = value / 100.

column1: Image Arrangement and Layout
column29: As a Document Author, I want to control how images are positioned, wrapped, aligned, and layered within the document, so that images integrate properly with surrounding text and content.
column363:
h3. AC 4.1: Wrap Mode

* Wrap Text dropdown: 9 modes with checkmark. Inline: inline-block, float none, vertical-align middle, margin 8px 0.

* Square/Tight: inline-block, float left, margin 8px auto. WrapLeft: block, float left, margin 0 16px 8px 0. WrapRight: block, float right, margin 0 0 8px 16px.

* Center: block, float none, margin 8px auto. BehindText: position absolute, z-index −1. InFrontOfText: position absolute, z-index 10.

* Changes take effect immediately.

h3. AC 4.2: Page Position

* Position dropdown: 3×3 grid (9 positions). Click toggles on/off (dark filled). “Clear” link when active.

* Left column: float left. Center: float none, margin auto. Right: float right. Bottom row: clear both.

* Ribbon button active when position ≠ none.

h3. AC 4.3: Alignment

* Align dropdown: Horizontal (Left/Center/Right) and Vertical (Top/Middle/Bottom) with checkmarks.

h3. AC 4.4: Layer Order

* Bring Fwd dropdown: Bring Forward (z+1), Bring to Front (z = max+1). Send Bwd: Send Backward (z−1), Send to Back (z = min−1).

* Also in Selection Pane and properties Arrange card (4 buttons + z-order display + reset).

* Info toast after each change.

h3. AC 4.5: Drag-and-Drop Repositioning

* Drag selected image: HTML drag API, MIME type application/x-rainbow-image-id.

* Drop cursor: 3 px blue line + 2 px ring shadow between content blocks.

* Drop: image removed from original, spliced to new position. “Image repositioned” toast.

h3. AC 4.6: Arrow Key Nudging

* Arrow keys: nudge 1 px. Shift+arrow: 10 px. Stored as nudgeX/nudgeY via CSS translate.

* Suppressed in input/textarea.

column1: Image Manipulation (Resize, Rotate, Crop, Flip)
column29: As a Document Author, I want to resize, rotate, crop, and flip images directly on the canvas using interactive handles and controls, so that I can adjust image presentation without external tools.
column363:
h3. AC 3.1: Image Selection Chrome

* Single-click: 2 px solid dark outline (#18181b), 2 px offset. 8 resize handles + rotate handle + Crop button below.

* Figure: draggable=true, tabIndex=0, title=altText.

h3. AC 3.2: Resize Handles

* Corners (nw/ne/se/sw): offset −5 px, cursor nwse/nesw-resize. Edges (n/s/e/w): centered midpoints, cursor ns/ew-resize.

* 10×10 px elements, class img-resize-handle. Only shown when selected and not in crop mode.

* Corner drag + locked ratio: proportional resize, dominant axis. Corner drag + unlocked/Shift: independent.

* Edge drag + locked: perpendicular adjusts proportionally. Edge drag + unlocked: single axis.

* Min: 60 px width, 40 px height. Resize is live (every mousemove).

* Ribbon/properties numeric inputs: commit on Enter/Tab. Invalid value reverts. Locked ratio adjusts other dimension.

h3. AC 3.3: Rotate Handle

* Stem: 1 px wide, 32 px tall, zinc-400 at rest, zinc-900 during drag. Grab: 18×18 px circle, white fill + zinc-400 border at rest; zinc-900 fill + border + ring shadow during drag. Small curved-arrow SVG icon inside.

* Positioned: horizontal center, 50 px above image. overflow:visible on figure. Pointer events: none on container, all on grab only.

* Drag: angle computed via atan2 from image center. Updates every mousemove. Dark pill tooltip shows angle (e.g., “45°”).

* Shift: snaps to 15°. Angle normalized 0–359°, rounded to integer. Hover: border darkens + shadow intensifies. Cursor: grab.

* Also settable via ribbon Rotate dropdown (90° L/R, 180°) and properties panel exact-angle input (0–359°).

h3. AC 3.4: Flip

* Flip Horizontal: scaleX(-1). Flip Vertical: scaleY(-1). Toggles with checkmark. Composable with rotation.

* Reset all in Rotate dropdown: rotation 0°, both flips cleared.

h3. AC 3.5: Crop Mode — Entry and Exit

* Entry: Crop button below image or ribbon Size group. Outline changes to orange, cursor to crosshair, resize/rotate handles hidden.

* Crop toolbar (below image, centered): Reset, Cancel (✕), Done (✓ orange). Escape = Cancel. Click outside = Cancel.

* Done: commits crop. Cancel: reverts. Reset (in crop mode): clears edges to 0% but stays in crop mode.

h3. AC 3.6: Crop Overlay and Handles

* Overlay: 4 semi-transparent black regions + 2 px orange border on visible area + rule-of-thirds gridlines (white 25% opacity).

* Percentage badge (top-left): “X% × Y%.” Only when width > 40 px and height > 20 px.

* Edge handles (4): circular 10×10 px, orange + 2 px white border. ns-resize (top/bottom), ew-resize (left/right). Single-edge drag.

* Corner handles (4): square 14×14 px, orange + 2 px white border, border-radius 2 px. nwse/nesw-resize. Dual-edge drag.

* Constraints: opposing edges sum ≤ 90% (min 10% visible per axis). Values rounded to integer %.

h3. AC 3.7: Crop Data Model and Rendering

* Non-destructive: ImageCrop stores top/right/bottom/left (0–50%). Src never modified.

* Render: wrapper div sized to visible %, img offset by negative top/left, wrapper overflow:hidden.

* Ribbon Crop button: “Re-Crop” label + active state when crop applied. Reset Crop button appears when active.
* Reset from: ribbon Reset Crop, properties Crop card Reset, crop toolbar Reset.

column1: Image Property Editing
column29: As a Document Author, I want to edit image properties such as corrections, border, caption, alt text, dimensions, opacity, and hyperlink, so that I can fine-tune each image’s appearance and metadata to meet document standards and accessibility requirements.
column363:
h3. AC 2.1: Picture Format Ribbon — Display and Dismissal

* Image selected (single-click): Picture Format ribbon replaces standard Toolbar. Header shows “Picture Format” tab indicator (dark filled, Image icon, vertical divider).

* Ribbon groups: Adjust, Picture Styles, Arrange, Size, and far-right Delete. Each with uppercase label at bottom.

* Each button: icon on top, label below, optional chevron for dropdowns.

* Image deselected: standard Toolbar restored, tab indicator removed.

h3. AC 2.2: Corrections (Brightness, Contrast, Sharpness)

* Corrections dropdown: three sliders — Brightness (0–200%, default 100%), Contrast (0–200%, default 100%), Sharpness (0–10, default 0).

* Each slider: monospace value display, per-slider reset button when non-default.

* Changes update CSS filter immediately: brightness(%), contrast(%), blur(px).

* Any non-default: “Reset all” link at bottom. Ribbon button shows active (filled) state.

h3. AC 2.3: Color / Saturation

* Color dropdown: Saturation slider (0–200%, default 100%) + five presets (B&W 0%, 50%, Original 100%, 150%, 200%).

* Preset click snaps slider. Active preset shows filled dark style. CSS saturate filter updates immediately.

* Ribbon button active when saturation ≠ 100%.

h3. AC 2.4: Transparency / Opacity

* Transparency dropdown: Opacity slider (10–100%, default 100%) + four presets (100%, 75%, 50%, 25%).

* CSS opacity updates immediately (opacity = value / 100). Ribbon button active when opacity ≠ 100%.

h3. AC 2.5: Reset Picture

* Reset button: restores corrections to defaults (brightness 100, contrast 100, sharpness 0, saturation 100), opacity to 100, removes border, restores originalWidth/originalHeight.

* Disabled (greyed out, cursor not-allowed) when all values at defaults.

h3. AC 2.6: Picture Border

* Border dropdown: “Enable border” checkbox. On enable: width 1 px, color #71717a, style solid.

* Controls: Width input (1–20 px), Color picker + hex code, 4-button style grid (Solid/Dashed/Dotted/Double) with live preview lines.

* Active style button: filled dark. CSS border updates immediately. Disable removes border.

* Ribbon button active when border enabled. Live swatch badge in dropdown header.

h3. AC 2.7: Alt Text and Accessibility

* Alt Text dropdown: “Mark as decorative” checkbox + textarea (placeholder: “Describe this image for screen readers…”).

* Decorative checked: textarea hidden, altText cleared, image renders empty alt. Unchecked: previously saved alt text restored.

* Typing updates altText immediately. Ribbon button active when alt text non-empty or decorative checked.

h3. AC 2.8: Caption

* Caption text input in properties panel. Non-empty: figcaption renders below image + format controls (Bold B, Italic I, font size 9–14 px, default 11 px).

* Bold/Italic toggles: filled dark state when active. Font size changes immediately. Stored in captionFormat.

* Empty caption: figcaption removed, format controls hidden. Caption not shown in crop mode.

h3. AC 2.9: Image Link

* URL input in Link card. Non-empty: image wraps in anchor (target=_blank, rel=noopener noreferrer). Empty: no anchor.

* Non-https URL: warning “⚠ URL should begin with https://.” Link click prevented in editor (e.preventDefault).

* Link wrapping not applied during crop mode.

h3. AC 2.10: Image Properties Panel (Sidebar)

* Double-click image: right sidebar opens on Properties tab. Thumbnail strip: preview (56×40 px), caption/“No caption,” dimensions (“· cropped” if active).

* Card sections: Accessibility, Caption, Dimensions, Adjust, Picture Border, Arrange, Crop (orange accent with before/after preview), Link, Actions.

* Dimensions card: Width/Height inputs (own rows), Lock aspect ratio checkbox + icon. Commit on blur/Enter.

* Adjust card: 4 correction sliders + Transparency slider, per-slider reset, top-level Reset button (disabled when unmodified).

* Crop card: 4 edge sliders with range + numeric input, Active badge, Reset button, real-time preview.

* Actions: “Replace Image” button + “Delete Image” (red, confirmation). No image selected: empty state.

h3. AC 2.11: Delete Image (Ribbon)

* Delete button at far-right of ribbon, separated by border. Trash icon + “Delete” label in destructive style.
* Click shows browser confirmation dialog. On confirm: image deleted, selection cleared, sidebar closed, “Image deleted” toast.

column1: Image Insertion
column29: As a Document Author, I want to insert images into my document from multiple sources (file upload, URL, and a reusable document library), so that I can add visual content quickly regardless of where the image originates.
column363:
h3. AC 1.1: Insert Image Dialog — General Behavior

* When the user clicks Insert > Image > Upload from Computer in the header menu, the Insert Image dialog opens on the Upload tab.

* When the user clicks Insert > Image > Insert from URL in the header menu, the Insert Image dialog opens on the From URL tab.

* When the user clicks Insert > Image > Search Stock Images in the header menu, the Insert Image dialog opens on the Library tab.

* When the user clicks the Insert Image button in the toolbar, the Insert Image dialog opens on the Upload tab.

* When the dialog opens, it displays as a centered modal overlay with a semi-transparent black backdrop.

* When the user clicks the backdrop, the X button, or presses Escape, the dialog closes.

* The dialog has three tabs: Upload (Upload icon), From URL (Link icon), Document Library (Library icon + badge showing library count).

* When the user clicks a tab, the corresponding panel displays and the active tab shows a dark bottom-border indicator.

* The dialog title reads “Insert Image” in Insert mode and “Replace Image” in Replace mode.

* The dialog subtitle reads “Upload from your device, paste a URL, or pick from your document library.” in Insert mode and “Choose a replacement — position, size and wrapping are preserved.” in Replace mode.

h3. AC 1.2: Upload Tab — File Selection and Drag-and-Drop

* When the Upload tab is active, a dashed-border drop zone is displayed with an upload icon, “Drag & drop image files here” text, and “or click to browse” helper text.

* When the user clicks the drop zone, a native file picker opens accepting PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG, and BMP files.

* In Insert mode the file picker allows multiple file selection (multiple=true). In Replace mode only single file selection (multiple=false).

* When the user drags files over the drop zone, the border changes to solid dark and the background tints to indicate active drag-over.

* Accepted MIME types: image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp, image/svg+xml, image/bmp.

* Format info displayed: “PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG, BMP · Max 25 MB · Max 8,000 × 8,000 px.”

* In Insert mode additional text: “Multiple files supported · Auto-saved to Document Library.”

* A persistent amber info box: “Note: TIFF and RAW formats are not supported. Convert to PNG or JPEG before uploading.”

h3. AC 1.3: Upload Tab — Validation and Error Handling

* When a file has an unsupported MIME type, an inline error card appears: “[filename]: Unsupported format.”

* When a file exceeds 25 MB, an inline error card appears: “[filename]: Too large ([size] MB). Max 25 MB.”

* When a file exceeds 8,000 px on either dimension, an inline error card appears: “[filename]: Exceeds 8,000×8,000 px max.”

* When a file cannot be read, an inline error card appears: “[filename]: Could not read image.” or “[filename]: Failed to read.”

* Multiple error cards can be shown simultaneously for multi-file uploads.

* While files are being validated, a spinner with “Processing…” is displayed.

* After all files processed, success confirmation: “Image inserted and saved to library.” or “N images inserted and saved to library.”

h3. AC 1.4: Upload Tab — Insertion Behavior

* Valid files are read as base64 data URIs via FileReader.

* If natural width exceeds 560 px, display width is capped at 560 px with height scaled proportionally. Otherwise original dimensions are used.

* Original dimensions stored in originalWidth and originalHeight for Reset.

* New ImageItem created with defaults: wrapMode Inline, alignment Left, lockAspectRatio true, opacity 100, border null, linkUrl empty, corrections at defaults, rotation 0, crop none.

* Image inserted at current cursor position (cursorAfterContentIdRef).

* Image auto-added to Document Library with unique ID, base64 src, filename, natural dimensions, timestamp.

* After insertion the image is selected and Picture Format ribbon activates. “Image inserted” toast appears.

* In Insert mode dialog stays open (user clicks Done). In Replace mode / URL / Library tabs dialog auto-closes.

h3. AC 1.5: From URL Tab

* URL input with placeholder “[https://example.com/image.png.”|https://example.com/image.png.”] Helper text: “Must begin with https://.”

* Empty URL + Preview: error “Please enter a URL.” Non-https URL: error “URL must begin with https://.”

h3. AC 1.6: Document Library Tab

* Empty library: ImageOff icon, “Library is empty,” “Images you upload are automatically saved here for reuse,” “Add first image” button.

* Hover shows delete button (trash icon) in top-left. Click deletes item from library.

* Search filters by name (case-insensitive). No matches: “No results for [query]” + “Clear search” link.

* “Add to Library” opens file picker to add images directly to library.

* Triggered via context menu, ribbon Change button, or properties panel Replace button.

* After replacement: image selected, “Image replaced” toast, dialog closes, Replace state cleared.

* Upload tab: auto-added after validation. URL tab: added if checkbox checked. Deduplication by src.

column29:
As an *Integration Admin with data source management privileges*, I want to *permanently delete an inactive data source from the platform with a confirmation step*, so that *I can remove obsolete or incorrectly configured data sources and keep the integration registry clean, with the assurance that active data flows have already been stopped before removal*.

Attached the functional spec along with screenshots. Also, attached the prototype to production document which might be useful if we are using our prototype source code.
column363:
h3. AC1: Delete Menu Option — Inactive Source (Enabled)

* When a data source is *Inactive*, the *"Delete"* option in the context menu is enabled (red text, clickable).

* The option is positioned as the last item in the context menu.

* The option uses destructive text treatment to signal a permanent action.

h3. AC2: Delete Menu Option — Active Source (Disabled)

* When a data source is *Active*, the *"Delete"* option in the context menu is visible but disabled (grayed out, non-clickable).

* Hovering over the disabled option displays a tooltip: *"Deactivate the data source before deleting."*

* Clicking the disabled option has no effect — no modal is opened.

h3. AC3: Context Menu Gating During Refresh

* When the data source’s refresh status is *In Progress*, the entire context menu trigger button is disabled and not clickable, regardless of active status.

h3. AC4: Delete Confirmation Modal Display

* When the user clicks the enabled *"Delete"* option (Inactive source), a centered modal overlay appears with a backdrop.

* The modal title reads *"Delete Data Source?"*.

* A warning/caution icon with destructive treatment is displayed above the title.

* The message body contains: "Data source *[Source Name]* will no longer be available once deleted."

* A second message reads: "You have to reconfigure if you need this data source in future."

* A confirmation prompt *"Please confirm."* is displayed with emphasis.

* Two action buttons are present: *"Cancel"* (secondary) and *"Delete"* (primary).

h3. AC5: Deletion Execution

* When the user clicks *"Delete"* on the confirmation modal, the data source is permanently removed from the system.

* The data source row disappears from the list screen immediately.

* The total source count on the list screen decrements by one.

* The modal closes after confirmation.

h3. AC6: Period Data Removal

* All periods belonging to the deleted data source are removed along with the source.

* Period record counts, preview data, sync history, and all associated metadata are deleted.

* No period data is archived or backed up as part of the delete operation.

h3. AC7: Cancel and Dismissal

* Clicking *"Cancel"* on the delete modal closes the modal with no state changes.

* The data source remains in the list with all its data intact after cancellation.

* Clicking outside the modal (on the backdrop) does not dismiss it — the user must explicitly choose Cancel or Delete.

h3. AC8: Two-Step Safeguard (Deactivate Then Delete)

* A user cannot delete an Active data source directly. The system enforces a two-step process: *Deactivate* first (which locks all periods and stops data flows), then *Delete*.

* This ensures the user has observed the impact of disabling the source before committing to permanent removal.

* The deactivation step is covered by the *Activate/Deactivate Data Source* spec.

h3. AC9: Irreversibility

* Once deletion is confirmed, there is no undo, restore, or trash mechanism.

* Recreating the same data source requires starting from scratch via the Create Data Source flow.

* No configuration backup or export is provided prior to deletion.

h3. AC10: Downstream Repository Impact

* Deleting a data source does not automatically delete or deactivate any downstream repository linked to it.

* Downstream repositories that previously referenced the deleted source must be notified or updated to reflect the missing upstream dependency.

h3. AC11: Access Control

* *Only users with data source management privileges* can see and use the Delete menu option.

* Users without the required privilege do not see the Delete option in the context menu.
