Display Contextual Feedback Messages Across All Comparison Workflows
column29:
_As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_see clear, contextual feedback messages when I encounter errors, when the system is processing, and when results are empty or successful_*_, so that_ *_I always understand what went wrong, what’s happening, or what to do next_*_._



h2. Message Reference Table

The following table lists every feedback message the system must display, organized by category. Each message has a unique ID, the trigger scenario, the exact message text, the display mechanism, and the screen where it appears.

 

h3. Validation Error Messages

|*ID*|*Trigger Scenario*|*Message Text*|*Display Type*|*Screen / Location*|
|ERR-01|User clicks Compare without selecting both source and target versions|"Select both source and target versions before running compare."|Inline error banner (red)|Compare Workspace → Settings panel (top)|
|ERR-02|User clicks Compare with all sheets excluded from scope|"Include at least one sheet before running workbook compare."|Inline error banner (red)|Compare Workspace → Settings panel (top)|
|ERR-03|User clicks Quick Run in Scope Dialog with no sheets selected|"Choose at least one sheet before running compare."|Inline error banner (red)|Version Selection Screen → Selection card|
|ERR-04|User clicks Open Compare with same version as source and target, or without both assigned|"Choose different source and target versions before opening compare."|Inline error banner (red)|Version Selection Screen → Selection card|
|ERR-05|User clicks Advanced Setup in Scope Dialog with no sheets selected|"Choose at least one sheet before opening advanced compare."|Inline error banner (red)|Version Selection Screen → Selection card|
|ERR-06|User changes a version in the workspace header such that source = target|"Source and target versions must be different."|Inline error banner (red)|Compare Workspace → Settings panel (top)|
|ERR-07|Comparison engine throws an unexpected/unhandled error|"Unable to run compare right now."|Inline error banner (red)|Compare Workspace → Settings panel (top)|

 

h3. Progress / Processing Messages

|*ID*|*Trigger Scenario*|*Message Text*|*Display Type*|*Screen / Location*|
|PRG-01|Comparison execution begins|"Comparing Versions..."|Modal dialog overlay — title|Full-screen overlay (ProgressOverlay)|
|PRG-02|Comparison execution in progress (dynamic detail)|"Analyzing {N} sheet{s} for changes"|Modal dialog overlay — subtitle|Full-screen overlay (ProgressOverlay)|
|PRG-03|Comparison progress updates|"{N}% complete"|Modal dialog overlay — below progress bar|Full-screen overlay (ProgressOverlay)|

 

h3. Empty State Messages

|*ID*|*Trigger Scenario*|*Message Text*|*Display Type*|*Screen / Location*|
|EMP-01|Results panel displayed before any comparison has been run|"Run a comparison to see workbook, row, column, and cell results here."|Dashed-border placeholder with icon|Compare Workspace → Results tab|
|EMP-02|No source version assigned yet in version selection|"Not selected" with helper text "Choose a version from the list below"|Muted text in assignment summary|Version Selection Screen → Source slot|
|EMP-03|No target version assigned yet in version selection|"Select A Version To Compare With" with helper text "This will be considered as the Base version"|Muted text in assignment summary|Version Selection Screen → Target slot|

 

h3. Success / Result State Messages

|*ID*|*Trigger Scenario*|*Message Text*|*Display Type*|*Screen / Location*|
|SUC-01|Comparison completes and zero diffs are found (single sheet or non-multi-sheet scope)|"No differences found. The selected versions match for this scope."|Green-bordered success card|Compare Workspace → Results tab|
|SUC-02|Comparison completes, zero diffs found on the currently active sheet in multi-sheet mode|"No differences found for this sheet."|Green-bordered success card|Compare Workspace → Results tab|
|SUC-03|Comparison completes with diffs found — summary strip|"{N} change{s}" (total count) displayed in the results header alongside per-category badges (e.g., "5 Edited", "2 Rows+")|Text label + colored badges|Compare Workspace → Results tab header + summary strip|
column363:
*AC-7.1.1: Inline Validation Error Display*

* When the user triggers a validation error (ERR-01 through ERR-07), the corresponding error message is displayed as an inline red-bordered banner at the top of the Settings panel (in the Compare Workspace) or within the selection card (on the Version Selection Screen).

* The error banner has a red border (border-red-200), a light red background (bg-red-50), and red text (text-red-700).

* Only one error banner is visible at a time. A new error replaces any previously displayed error.

* When the user takes a corrective action (e.g., selects a different version, includes a sheet, navigates away), the error banner is cleared.

 

*AC-7.1.2: Error Clearance on State Change*

* When the user changes the source or target version selection, any displayed error is cleared (compareError is reset to empty string).

* When the user navigates from the Version Selection Screen to the Compare Workspace, any displayed error is cleared.

* When the user clicks Reset in the Settings panel, any displayed error is cleared.

* When the user opens the Scope Dialog, any displayed error is cleared.

 

*AC-7.1.3: Progress Overlay During Comparison Execution*

* When the user clicks Compare (quick or advanced), a full-screen modal overlay appears displaying PRG-01 as the title, PRG-02 as the subtitle with the dynamic sheet count, and PRG-03 as the progress percentage below an animated progress bar.

* The progress bar advances through timed steps (12% → 28% → 44% → 59% → 73% → 86% → 100%) at ~140ms intervals to provide perceived responsiveness.

* The overlay includes a centered icon (GitCompareArrows) inside a rounded primary-colored circle.

* The overlay is non-interactive — the user cannot dismiss or cancel it.

* When progress reaches 100%, the overlay fades out after a ~220ms delay before transitioning to the Results tab.

 

*AC-7.1.4: Empty State Before Comparison*

* When the Results tab is displayed and no comparison has been run, the system shows message EMP-01 inside a dashed-border placeholder card with a centered icon (ArrowLeftRight) at reduced opacity.

* This placeholder is replaced by the diff list once a comparison completes.

 

*AC-7.1.5: Empty State for Version Assignment*

* When no source version is assigned, the assignment summary panel shows EMP-02 — "Not selected" with the helper text "Choose a version from the list below".

* When no target version is assigned, the assignment summary panel shows EMP-03 — "Select A Version To Compare With" with the helper text "This will be considered as the Base version".

* When both versions are assigned, the helper texts are replaced by the version labels and timestamps.

 

*AC-7.1.6: Zero Diffs Result State*

* When a comparison completes with zero diffs in a non-multi-sheet scope, the Results tab shows message SUC-01 inside a green-bordered card (border-emerald-300, bg-emerald-50, text-emerald-700).

* When viewing a specific sheet in multi-sheet mode and that sheet has zero diffs, the Results tab shows message SUC-02 inside the same green-bordered card style.

* The green success card replaces the diff list area. Filter tabs are not displayed when there are zero diffs.

 

*AC-7.1.7: Summary Results Feedback*

* When a comparison completes with one or more diffs, the Results tab header shows SUC-03 — the total change count as "{N} change{s}" (singular/plural).

* Below the filter tabs, a summary strip displays compact color-coded badges for each non-zero diff category: "N Edited" (amber), "N Added" (green), "N Removed" (red), "N Rows+" (blue), "N Rows-" (pink), "N Reordered" (indigo), "N Type" (cyan), "N Sheets+" (green), "N Sheets-" (red), "N Changed Sheets" (slate).

* Only categories with a count greater than zero are shown. Empty categories are hidden.

* In multi-sheet mode, the summary strip reflects the active sheet’s diff counts, not the entire workbook’s totals.

column1: Feedback Messages & System States
column29:
_Provide clear, contextual feedback to the user across all comparison workflows — including validation errors, progress indicators, empty states, and success confirmations — so that the user always understands the system’s current state and any required actions_

h2.

column1: Workspace Version Switching, Reset, and Navigation
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_change versions, reset settings, and navigate within the workspace_*_, so that_ *_I can iterate without returning to the selection screen_*_._
column363:
*AC-6.2.1: Version Switching*

* The header bar shows Source and Target version pills with dropdown changers.

* When the user selects a different version, the system validates that source ≠ target.

* All comparison results are cleared, settings reset to defaults, sheet configs re-initialized with auto-mapping, and the Settings tab activates.

* If source = target, an error message is displayed.

*AC-6.2.2: Swap Versions*

* The swap button (⇄) between the version pills exchanges source and target assignments.

* This triggers the same reset behavior as a version change.

*AC-6.2.3: Reset Settings*

* The Reset button (↺) reverts all settings to defaults: headerRows=[0], keyColumn=0, normalization defaults, per-sheet configs.

* Existing comparison results are NOT cleared by Reset.

* Any active selection mode (row/column picking) is cancelled.

*AC-6.2.4: Back Navigation*

* The Back button (←) returns to the Version Selection Screen.

* All comparison state is cleared (results, highlights, selection mode).

*AC-6.2.5: Navigation Arrows*

* The previous (←) and next (→) arrows in the header navigate sequentially through the diff list items.

Each navigation step selects the next/previous diff and triggers click-to-focus behavior

column1: Export Comparison Results
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_export the comparison results as a downloadable file_*_, so that_ *_I can share findings with stakeholders or archive for compliance_*_._
column363:
*AC-6.1.1: Export Trigger*

* The workspace header shows an "Export" button.

* Clicking it opens a format selection (Excel / CSV / PDF).

*AC-6.1.2: Export Content*

* The export includes all diffs from the current comparison result (not filtered by the active tab).

* Export metadata includes: source version label, target version label, comparison timestamp, settings used, and summary statistics.

*AC-6.1.3: Export Formats*

* Excel (.xlsx): Multi-sheet workbook with source data, target data, and diff summary. Diff cells are highlighted.

* CSV (.csv): Flat diff list with columns: Sheet, Row, Column, Status, Old Value, New Value, Source Type, Target Type.

* PDF (.pdf): Formatted report with summary statistics and diff table.

column1: Export & Workspace Controls
column29: _Enable exporting comparison results, switching versions within the workspace, resetting settings, and managing toolbar controls._

column1: View a Past Comparison
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_reopen a past comparison and see its full results without re-running_*_, so that_ *_I save time and can review historical comparisons_*_._
column363:
*AC-5.3.1: Restore Full State*

* When the user clicks "View Comparison" on a past entry, the system restores: version selections, settings, per-sheet configurations, workbook defaults, and the cached comparison result.

* The Compare Workspace opens with the Results tab active.

* The active sheet is set to the first sheet with differences.

* Spreadsheet highlights are applied from the cached result.

*AC-5.3.2: Restored State Behavior*

* The restored comparison is fully interactive: click-to-focus, filtering, diffs-only toggle, and sheet switching all work on the cached data.

* The user can re-run the comparison with the restored settings by switching to Advanced mode and clicking Compare.

column1: Browse Past Comparisons
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_browse a list of my previous comparisons_*_, so that_ *_I can find and revisit a specific comparison_*_._
column363:
*AC-5.2.1: Past Comparisons Tab*

* The Version Selection Screen has a "Past Comparisons" tab alongside "Create New Compare".

* The tab displays a scrollable list of comparison history entries.

*AC-5.2.2: History Entry Display*

* Each entry shows: title, mode badge (Quick / Advanced), scope badge (Entire Workbook / N Sheets), visibility badge (Shared / Private), total change count, timestamp, and creator name.

* Each entry shows a "Changed Sheets" count.

* Entries created by other users show "Shared by [name]" instead of "Created by [name]".

*AC-5.2.3: Visibility Toggle*

* Each entry has a visibility dropdown (Private / Shared).

* Changing visibility updates the entry’s metadata.

column1: Auto-Save Comparison to History
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_have my comparisons automatically saved after execution_*_, so that_ *_I have an audit trail without manual effort_*_._
column363:
*AC-5.1.1: History Entry Creation*

* When a comparison completes (quick or advanced), a history entry is automatically created.

* The entry captures: unique ID, title ("[Source Label] vs [Target Label]"), version IDs, scope, included sheets, full settings snapshot, per-sheet configs, cached result, mode, owner name, and timestamp.

* The entry is prepended to the history list (most recent first).

*AC-5.1.2: History Capacity*

* The history list holds a maximum of 12 entries.

* When a new entry is added and the list exceeds 12, the oldest entry is removed.

* If the same comparison is re-run, the previous entry for that ID is replaced (not duplicated).

column1: Navigate to Diffs via Spreadsheet Cell Click
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_click a highlighted cell in the spreadsheet and see its diff in the results panel_*_, so that_ *_I can explore changes directly from the spreadsheet_*_._
column363:
*AC-4.3.1: Cell Click to Diff Selection*

* When the user clicks a highlighted (diffed) cell in either spreadsheet, the system identifies the matching diff in the results list.

* The matching diff item is selected and scrolled into view in the results list.

* The right pane switches to the Results tab if it was showing Settings.

column1: Navigate to Diffs via Click-to-Focus
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_click a diff item and have both spreadsheets scroll to the relevant cell_*_, so that_ *_I can see the change in context within the spreadsheet data_*_._
column363:
*AC-4.2.1: Cell-Level Diff Focus*

* When the user clicks a cell-level diff, both source and target spreadsheets scroll to the relevant cell.

* The focused cell receives a teal outline (diff-cell--focused) in both spreadsheets.

* The source focuses on the source row/column indices; the target focuses on the target row/column indices (which may differ when columns are reordered).

*AC-4.2.2: Row-Level Diff Focus*

* When the user clicks a row-inserted diff, the target spreadsheet scrolls to and highlights the entire inserted row.

* When the user clicks a row-deleted diff, the source spreadsheet scrolls to and highlights the entire deleted row.

*AC-4.2.3: Column/Structure Diff Focus*

* When the user clicks a column-deleted diff, the source spreadsheet highlights the deleted column.

* When the user clicks a column-new diff, the target spreadsheet highlights the new column.

* When the user clicks a column-reorder diff, both spreadsheets scroll to the header row (row 0).

*AC-4.2.4: Focus Lifecycle*

* When the user clicks a different diff item, the previous focus highlight is removed before the new one is applied.

* When switching sheets (via diff click on a different sheet), the sheet switches first, then the focus is applied after a short delay.

column1: View and Filter Comparison Results
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_see all differences categorized and filterable by type_*_, so that_ *_I can focus on specific types of changes_*_._
column363:
*AC-4.1.1: Results Tab Layout*

* When comparison completes, the Results tab shows: a filter tab bar, a summary strip, and a scrollable diff list.

* The filter tabs are: All (all diff types), Edited (cell-level modified/new/deleted/type-changed/fuzzy-match diffs), Rows+ (row-inserted diffs), Rows− (row-deleted diffs), Reordered (column-reorder and column-diff entries).

* Each tab shows a count badge with the number of diffs in that category.

* When results are active, the target spreadsheet pane receives a distinct amber/gold border accent to visually distinguish it from the source pane and signal that comparison results are being displayed.

*AC-4.1.2: Summary Strip*

* Below the filter tabs, compact inline badges show counts per diff type (e.g., "5 Edited", "2 Rows+", "1 Reordered").

* Only categories with non-zero counts are displayed.

* In multi-sheet mode, the summary shows counts for the active sheet only.

*AC-4.1.3: Diff List Items*

* Each diff item shows: a color-coded status badge (Edited, Row Added, Row Removed, Reordered, etc.), the sheet name, the location (column name in Row N), and old → new values.

* Values are displayed in their normalized form (e.g., "$220.00" appears as "220").

* Row-level diffs show a preview of the first 5 non-empty cell values joined by " | ".

*AC-4.1.4: Filter Behavior*

* When a filter tab is selected, the diff list shows only diffs matching that category.

* The "All" tab shows every diff regardless of type.

* Switching tabs preserves the selected diff item if it remains visible.

column1: Automatic or manual refresh of data source from external systems
column29:
As an *Integration Admin*, I want the system to *automatically refresh data for all Open periods on my Automatic Import data sources at the configured schedule, retry on failure, and notify me if the refresh persistently fails*, so that *period data stays current without manual intervention, and I am alerted promptly when action is needed*.

As an *Integration Admin*, I also want to *manually trigger a refresh for any individual Open period via the context menu*, so that *I can fetch updated data on demand between scheduled runs or when scheduled import is disabled*.

Attached the functional spec along with screenshots. Also, attached the prototype to production document which might be useful if we are using our prototype source code.

The screens are already covered in Create Data Source story. This is about conditions and behavior based on configuration for automatic import scenario
column363:
h3. AC1: Scheduled Refresh Trigger Conditions

* Scheduled refresh triggers when: refresh mode is Automatic Import, Enable Scheduled Import is ON, data source is Active, current time matches the configured schedule, and no refresh is currently In Progress.

* If any condition is not met, the scheduled run does not trigger.

h3. AC2: Scope — Open Periods Only

* The scheduled refresh fetches data for all periods with status Open.

* *Locked periods are skipped* and not included in the refresh run.

* If all periods are Locked, the run completes immediately with no data fetched (logged in run history as “No Open periods”).

h3. AC3: Refresh Status — In Progress

* When a scheduled or manual refresh starts, the data source’s refresh status changes to *In Progress*.

* Each period being refreshed shows refresh status *In Progress* on its row.

h3. AC4: Successful Refresh

* On success, each refreshed period’s status changes to *Success*.

* Record count is updated with the newly fetched data.

* Preview data is refreshed.

* Last synced timestamp is updated.

* Data source refresh status changes to *Success* when all periods complete.

* Last refreshed timestamp on the data source is updated.

h3. AC5: Failed Refresh — Retry Logic

* When a fetch fails for a period, the system automatically retries up to 3 attempts.

* Only failed periods are retried. Successfully refreshed periods are not re-fetched.

* Retries use increasing backoff intervals (exact intervals are a production decision).

h3. AC6: Persistent Failure — Admin Notification

* If all 3 retry attempts fail for a period:

–       The period’s refresh status changes to *Failed*.

–       Error details are stored and visible in the period row’s Sync Activity area.

–       The data source’s refresh status changes to *Failed*.

–       *A notification is sent to all assigned admins* of the data source.

–       The notification includes: data source name, failed period label(s), error summary, and timestamp.

h3. AC7: Partial Success

* If some periods succeed and others fail in the same run:

–       Successfully refreshed periods retain their updated data and show Success status.

–       Failed periods show Failed status with error details.

–       The data source’s overall refresh status is *Failed* (indicating attention needed).

–       Admin notification is sent for the failed periods.

h3. AC8: Manual Refresh — Context Menu

* A *“Refresh”* option is present in the three-dot context menu on each period row.

* The Refresh option is available for Automatic Import data sources regardless of whether Enable Scheduled Import is on or off.

* Clicking Refresh triggers a data fetch for that single period only.

h3. AC9: Manual Refresh — Disabled States

* Refresh is *disabled* for Locked periods. Tooltip: “Unlock the period to refresh.”

* Refresh is *disabled* for periods with status In Progress. Tooltip: “Refresh already in progress.”

* Refresh is *disabled* when the data source is Inactive. Tooltip: “Activate the data source to refresh.”

h3. AC10: Manual Refresh — Execution

* Manual refresh follows the same fetch, success, failure, and retry logic as scheduled refresh.

* Manual refresh targets a single period, not all Open periods.

* A run history entry is recorded tagged as “Manual” trigger type.

h3. AC11: Overlap Protection

* If the scheduled run time arrives while a refresh is already In Progress for the data source, the scheduled run is skipped.

* The skipped run is recorded in run history with status Skipped and reason “Refresh already in progress.”

* The next scheduled run proceeds at the following scheduled time.

* *Manual refresh on a different period is NOT blocked* by a scheduled run or another manual refresh on a different period. Overlap protection applies at the data source level for scheduled runs only.

h3. AC12: Run History

* A run history is maintained per data source and accessible from the Period List screen.

* *Each run history entry includes:*

–       Run timestamp (start time)

–       Trigger type: *Scheduled* or *Manual*

–       Periods included and periods skipped (Locked)

–       Status: *Success*, *Partial Failure*, *Failed*, or *Skipped*

–       Run duration

–       Error details and retry count (for failed runs)

h3. AC13: Run History — Drill-down

* User can click into a run history entry to see details.

* For failed runs, the drill-down shows which periods failed, the error messages, and how many retries were attempted.

h3. AC14: Deactivated Data Source

* *Inactive data sources are excluded from all scheduled runs.*

* If a data source is deactivated while a refresh is In Progress, the in-progress run completes but no further scheduled runs trigger.

* When reactivated, scheduled runs resume from the next scheduled time. No catch-up runs for missed schedules.

h3. AC15: Enable Scheduled Import Toggle

* *Toggle ON:* Scheduled runs are active and trigger at the configured schedule.

* *Toggle OFF:* Scheduled runs stop. Configuration (frequency, time, timezone) is preserved. Manual Refresh via the three-dot menu remains available.

* Toggling OFF while a run is In Progress allows the current run to complete but prevents the next scheduled run.

h3. AC16: Access Control

* *Only users with data source management privileges* can trigger Manual Refresh.

* The Refresh option is hidden from users without the required privilege.

column1: Run Advanced Compare
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_run a comparison with my custom settings for header rows, key column, normalization, and per-sheet configuration_*_, so that_ *_the comparison uses my exact configuration_*_._
column363:
*AC-3.2.1: Advanced Mode Execution*

* When Advanced mode is selected and the user clicks "Compare", the engine uses the user’s configured settings.

* Per-sheet configurations (header rows, key column) override workbook defaults for each respective sheet.

* Normalization toggles and thresholds apply as workbook-level defaults.

*AC-3.2.2: Mapped Sheets Execution*

* When scope is "mapped-sheets", the engine builds virtual workbooks from the sheet mapping (each source sheet paired with its mapped target sheet).

* The comparison uses the source sheet name as the canonical sheet name in the result.

*AC-3.2.3: Validation Errors*

* When no sheets are included, the error "Include at least one sheet before running workbook compare" is displayed.

* When source and target versions are not both selected or are the same, the error "Select both source and target versions before running compare" is displayed.

*AC-3.2.4: Diff Classification*

* Cell value changed: status = "modified" (amber).

* Cell empty in source, has value in target: status = "new" (green).

* Cell has value in source, empty in target: status = "deleted" (red).

* Row in target but not source: status = "row-inserted" (blue).

* Row in source but not target: status = "row-deleted" (pink).

* Cell data type changed (e.g., number → date): status = "type-changed" (cyan).

* Text similar above threshold: status = "fuzzy-match" (purple).

* Columns reordered: type = "column-reorder" (purple).

* Column in target only: status = "new" column-diff. Column in source only: status = "deleted" column-diff.

* Sheet in target only: status = "sheet-added". Sheet in source only: status = "sheet-removed".

column1: Run Quick Compare
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_run a one-click comparison with default settings_*_, so that_ *_I can see results immediately without configuration overhead_*_._
column363:
*AC-3.1.1: Quick Mode Execution*

* When Quick mode is selected and the user clicks "Compare", the engine executes with default settings: headerRows=[0], keyColumn=0, headerMatch=true, normalizeDates=true, normalizeBooleans=false, normalizeCurrency=false, numericThreshold=0, fuzzyTextThreshold=0.

* No settings configuration is required before execution.

*AC-3.1.2: Progress Overlay*

* A full-screen overlay appears with an animated progress bar and contextual text (e.g., "Analyzing 3 sheets for changes").

* The progress bar advances through timed steps to provide perceived responsiveness.

* The overlay is non-cancellable.

*AC-3.1.3: Completion Transition*

* When the comparison completes, the overlay fades (after ~220ms delay).

* The right pane switches to the Results tab.

* The active sheet auto-navigates to the first sheet with differences (firstChangedSheetName).

* The comparison entry is saved to history.

column1: Define Comparison Scope
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_choose whether to compare the entire workbook, selected sheets, or a single sheet_*_, so that_ *_I can scope the comparison to what matters_*_._
column363:
*AC-2.5.1: Scope Options*

* The Scope Dialog (if triggered) offers three options: Entire Workbook, Selected Sheets, Single Sheet.

* Entire Workbook includes all sheets from both source and target.

* Selected Sheets shows a checklist of all available sheet names. At least one must be checked.

* Single Sheet compares only the currently active sheet.

*AC-2.5.2: Scope Actions*

* "Quick Run" executes the comparison immediately with default settings for the chosen scope.

* "Advanced Setup" opens the Compare Workspace in Advanced mode with the chosen scope, allowing further configuration before execution.

column1: Configure Data Normalization
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_enable or disable normalization rules for dates, booleans, and currency_*_, so that_ *_formatting differences do not produce false diffs_*_._
column363:
*AC-2.4.1: Normalization Toggles*

* The "Other" section (expandable) shows toggles for: Match columns by header name, Normalize dates, Normalize booleans, Normalize currency.

* Each toggle has a description explaining its effect.

* "Match columns by header name" defaults to ON. "Normalize dates" defaults to ON. "Normalize booleans" and "Normalize currency" default to OFF.

*AC-2.4.2: Date Normalization Behavior*

* When ON, "2024-01-15" and "Jan 15, 2024" produce no diff (both normalize to ISO 2024-01-15).

* When OFF, they produce a Modified diff (raw string comparison).

* Supported formats: ISO (YYYY-MM-DD), US slash (MM/DD/YYYY), EU dot (DD.MM.YYYY), named month (Jan 15, 2024 / 15 January 2024).

* Invalid dates (e.g., "2023-02-29" for a non-leap year) remain as text and are compared as strings.

*AC-2.4.3: Boolean Normalization Behavior*

* When ON, true/yes/y/1/on are treated as equal (all normalize to "true"). false/no/n/0/off are treated as equal (normalize to "false"). Case-insensitive.

* "1" is detected as a number (not boolean) due to type priority order. "1" vs "true" produces a type-changed diff.

*AC-2.4.4: Currency Normalization Behavior*

* When ON, currency symbols ($, €, £, ¥, ₹, ₩) and thousands-comma separators are stripped. "$1,200.50" equals "1200.5".

* When OFF, "$99.99" vs "99.99" produces a Modified diff.

*AC-2.4.5: Numeric Tolerance*

* A number input allows setting a tolerance threshold (default 0).

* When set to 0.05, values 36.60 and 36.61 (diff = 0.01) produce no diff. Values 50 and 55 (diff = 5.0) produce a Modified diff.

* Tolerance applies only to values detected as numeric type.

*AC-2.4.6: Text Similarity Threshold*

* A number input allows setting a similarity threshold from 0 to 0.99 (default 0).

* When set to 0.7, "Wireless Mouse" vs "Wireless Mice" (similarity ~0.80) is classified as Fuzzy Match. "Standing Desk" vs "Office Chair" (similarity ~0.15) is classified as Modified.

* The UI clamps the input to a maximum of 0.99. Setting 1.0 is rejected.

* Fuzzy matching applies only to text-type values. Numeric values use exact/tolerance comparison.

column1: Map Source Sheets to Target Sheets
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_map each source sheet to a specific target sheet_*_, so that_ *_I can compare sheets even when they have been renamed between versions_*_._
column363:
*AC-2.3.1: Sheet Mapping Dropdowns*

* In the workspace, the Settings panel shows "Source Sheet" and "Target" dropdowns for the active sheet.

* The Target dropdown lists all sheets from the target workbook.

* By default, sheets are matched by name. When names match, the dropdown pre-selects the matching target sheet.

*AC-2.3.2: Manual Remapping*

* When the user selects a different target sheet from the dropdown, the target spreadsheet pane reloads with the newly mapped sheet’s data.

* The mapping persists per source sheet and is used during comparison execution.

*AC-2.3.3: Sheet Include/Exclude*

* In workbook mode, the sheet list shows an include/exclude toggle per sheet.

* Excluded sheets are not sent to the comparison engine.

* At least one sheet must be included; attempting to compare with all sheets excluded shows an error.

column1: Designate Key Column for Row Matching
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_designate a column that uniquely identifies rows_*_, so that_ *_the engine matches rows by key value instead of position, correctly detecting insertions and deletions_*_._
column363:
*AC-2.2.1: Key Column Dropdown*

* The Settings panel shows a "Key Column For Matching" dropdown listing all columns by their header name (or composite header name).

* Selecting a column from the dropdown sets it as the key column for comparison.

*AC-2.2.2: Visual Column Selection*

* When the user clicks the pointer icon next to the key column picker, the source spreadsheet enters column-selection mode.

* The currently selected column is highlighted across all rows.

* When the user clicks any column in the source spreadsheet, the highlight moves and the dropdown updates.

* Confirm (✓) saves the selection; Cancel (✗) reverts it.

*AC-2.2.3: No Key Column (Positional Mode)*

* When the key column is set to "None", rows are compared by position (index).

* Inserting or removing a row in the middle causes cascading positional diffs for all subsequent rows.

column1: Select Header Rows
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_designate which spreadsheet rows contain column headers_*_, so that_ *_the engine correctly identifies column names for matching and display_*_._
column363:
*AC-2.1.1: Header Row Picker Display*

* The Settings panel shows a "Select header row" section with a dropdown for each configured header row slot.

* Each dropdown displays a row preview: "Row N — [first 4 cell values joined by ' | ']".

* A default single header row slot is pre-filled with Row 1 (index 0).

*AC-2.1.2: Visual Row Selection*

* When the user clicks the pointer icon (→) next to a header row picker, the source spreadsheet enters row-selection mode.

* The currently selected row is highlighted with a distinct selection background color.

* Other settings controls are dimmed during selection mode to focus attention.

* When the user clicks any data row in the source spreadsheet, the highlight moves to that row and the dropdown preview updates in real time.

* When the user clicks the confirm button (✓), the selected row index is saved and selection mode exits.

* When the user clicks the cancel button (✗), the selection reverts to the previous value and selection mode exits.

*AC-2.1.3: Multi-Row Composite Headers*

* When the user clicks "Add row" (⊕), a new header row slot is appended with the next unused row index.

* When multiple header rows are selected, the system builds composite headers by joining each column’s values with " | " (e.g., "Q1 | Revenue").

* The key column dropdown updates to show composite header labels.

*AC-2.1.4: Remove Header Row*

* When the user clicks the trash icon on a header row slot, that slot is removed.

* If the removed slot was in active selection mode, selection mode exits.

* If all header row slots are removed (headerRows = []), columns are labeled A, B, C and the "Match columns by header name" toggle is disabled.

column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_start a comparison directly from the host application’s Version History panel_*_, so that_ *_I can begin comparing without extra navigation_*_._
column363:

column1: Preview Version Data
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_preview a version’s spreadsheet data before selecting it_*_, so that_ *_I can confirm I have the correct version_*_._
column363:
*AC-1.3.1: Spreadsheet Preview*

* The left pane of the Version Selection Screen displays a read-only spreadsheet preview of the currently previewed version.

* The preview shows the workbook’s sheet tabs at the bottom (e.g., Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow).

* When the user clicks a sheet tab, the preview updates to show that sheet’s data.

*AC-1.3.2: Preview Version Context*

* The preview header shows the version label, timestamp, and a "Workbook Preview" badge.

* The preview automatically shows the target version when assigned, or the source version otherwise, or the most recent version as fallback.

column1: Assign Source and Target Versions
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_assign two different versions as source and target_*_, so that_ *_I can define which versions to compare_*_._
column363:
*AC-1.2.1: Version Assignment*

* Each version card shows a "Source" button and a "Target" button.

* When the user clicks "Source" on a version, that version is assigned as source. The button fills with a checkmark indicator.

* When the user clicks "Target" on a version, that version is assigned as target.

* When the same version is assigned to both roles, the conflicting (previous) assignment is automatically cleared.

*AC-1.2.2: Assignment Summary*

* A summary panel above the version list shows the currently assigned source and target with their labels and timestamps.

* When no source is assigned, the summary shows "Not selected" with helper text.

* When no target is assigned, the summary shows "Not selected" with helper text.

*AC-1.2.3: Compare Button State*

* The "Open Compare" button is disabled when source and target are not both assigned, or when they are the same version.

* The "Open Compare" button is enabled only when both are assigned and different.

* When the user clicks "Open Compare", the system navigates to the Compare Workspace.

column1: Browse and Filter Versions
column29: _As_ *_an analyst_*_, I want to_ *_browse all available workbook versions and filter by save type_*_, so that_ *_I can quickly find the specific version I need to compare_*_._
column363:
*AC-1.1.1: Version List Display*

* When the Version Selection Screen loads, the system displays all available workbook versions in a scrollable list.

* Each version card shows: version label, subtitle, timestamp, variant badge (Auto / Manual), author name with avatar, and a starred indicator for base versions.

* When viewing a specific version, the version header bar displays the version label, timestamp, and an auto-save reason badge (e.g., "Auto saved at Review Cycle Completion") describing the event that triggered the version creation.

* Versions are ordered by timestamp (most recent first).

*AC-1.1.2: Version Type Filtering*

* When the user clicks the "Auto-save" filter pill, only versions with variant = "auto" are displayed.

* When the user clicks the "Manual" filter pill, only versions with variant = "manual" are displayed.

* When the user clicks the "All" filter pill, all versions are displayed regardless of variant.

* The active filter pill is visually distinguished (filled background).

* A filter/sort icon (funnel) is displayed adjacent to the filter pills, providing additional sorting and filtering controls for the version list.

column1: Creation of period for automatic import scenario
column29:
As an *Integration Admin with data source management privileges*, I want to *create a new period for an Automatic Import data source — either by selecting from existing periods on other sources or by defining a new custom period — and have the system immediately fetch data from the connected external system*, so that *period data is available without waiting for the next scheduled import run, and downstream repositories receive timely responses to their data requests*.

Attached the functional spec along with screenshots. Also, attached the prototype to production document which might be useful if we are using our prototype source code.
column363:
h3. AC1: Entry Point — Toolbar

* For Automatic Import data sources, a *“Create Period”* button is displayed in the Period List toolbar.

* The button is enabled regardless of data source active status.

* Clicking opens the Create Period side panel in Mode A (existing period list).

h3. AC2: Entry Point — Requests Received Modal

* The Requests Received modal displays a *“Create Period”* button for requests targeting an Automatic Import data source.

* Clicking opens the Create Period dialog in Mode B with period dates pre-filled and read-only from the request.

* Mode A selection and “Back to Existing Periods” link are not shown when opened from a request.

h3. AC3: Mode A — Select from Existing Periods

* Mode A is the default view when the dialog opens from the toolbar.

* The dialog shows a list of periods from other data sources in the system (not the current data source).

* Each period in the list shows: period label, type, date range, and the name of the source it belongs to.

* A search field allows filtering the list by label or date.

* User selects a period and clicks “Create Period” to create a matching period on the current data source.

h3. AC4: Mode A → Mode B Navigation

* An *“Add New Period”* link is displayed below the existing period list in Mode A.

* Clicking the link switches the dialog to Mode B (create new period form).

h3. AC5: Mode B — Create New Period

* Mode B shows a form with: Period Type dropdown, date inputs, and optional Comments field.

* User fills in the period details and clicks “Create Period”.

h3. AC6: Mode B → Back to Mode A

* In Mode B, a *“Back to Existing Periods”* link is displayed.

* Clicking the link returns the dialog to Mode A.

* Any data entered in Mode B is discarded on navigation back.

* The “Back to Existing Periods” link is NOT shown when the dialog is opened from a request (pre-filled dates).

h3. AC7: Period Type Selection

* The Period Type dropdown offers: Range (Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly, Custom) and As-of.

* When the data source has no existing periods, the dropdown is enabled and the user can select any type.

* When the data source has existing periods, the dropdown is disabled and locked to the existing type. A helper text explains the restriction.

h3. AC8: Date Inputs — Shared Component

* Date inputs (start date, end date, as-of date) must use the shared date picker component.

* Range type shows Start Date and End Date fields.

* As-of type shows a single As-of Date field.

* When opened from a Requests Received modal, date fields are pre-filled and read-only. The user cannot change them.

h3. AC9: Comments Field

* An optional Comments field is present (maximum 300 characters).

* Content is stored as the period’s notes.

h3. AC10: No File Upload Section

* The Create Period dialog does not contain a file upload field.

* No file picker, drag-and-drop area, or format validation is shown.

* Data is fetched from the external system, not uploaded by the user.

h3. AC11: Duplicate Period Warning

* When the selected (Mode A) or entered (Mode B) dates match an existing period in the current data source, a confirmation modal appears before creation.

* *“Proceed”* creates the period, replacing any existing data.

* *“Cancel”* returns to the dialog with no changes.

h3. AC12: Period Created — Initial State

* On confirmation, the period is created with the selected/entered dates, status Open, record count 0, and no preview data.

* The dialog closes immediately after creation.

* The new period appears in the Period List with refresh status *In Progress*.

h3. AC13: Immediate Data Fetch Triggered

* Immediately after the period is created, the system sends a data fetch request to the relevant external system.

* The fetch uses the data source’s configured connection details (connection type, host URL, credentials, auth method, timeout, etc.).

* The fetch targets the date range of the newly created period.

* The period row displays refresh status *In Progress* during the fetch.

h3. AC14: Successful Data Fetch

* When the data fetch completes successfully, the period’s refresh status changes from In Progress to *Success*.

* The period’s record count is updated with the number of fetched records.

* Preview data is populated and accessible via the View Data action.

* The last synced timestamp is updated to the time the fetch completed.

h3. AC15: Failed Data Fetch

* When the data fetch fails, the period’s refresh status changes from In Progress to *Failed*.

* The period remains in the list with record count 0 and no preview data.

* Error details are visible in the Sync Activity area of the period row.

* The period is not automatically deleted on fetch failure.

* The user can retry the fetch from the period row context menu (covered in a separate spec).

h3. AC16: Request Fulfillment — Decision Point

* *Option A (prototype behaviour):* The period request is marked as Fulfilled when the period is created, regardless of whether the data fetch succeeds or fails.

* *Option B (production consideration):* The request is marked as Fulfilled only when the data fetch completes successfully.

* *Production decision required:* Confirm which option applies before implementation.

h3. AC17: On Repository Request — Auto-pull Behaviour

* When the data source is configured with *“Auto-pull from upstream system”* (repoPullBehavior setting):

* The system handles downstream repository requests automatically without user intervention.

* *No Requests Received badge* is shown on the Period List.

* The system automatically creates a period for the requested date range (if one does not already exist).

* The system immediately triggers a data fetch from the external system for the period.

* The period appears in the Period List with refresh status *In Progress*.

* The success/failure outcomes follow the same rules as manual creation (AC14, AC15).

* The request is fulfilled automatically based on the fulfillment policy (AC16).

h3. AC18: On Repository Request — Notify and Manually Trigger Behaviour

* When the data source is configured with *“Notify and manually trigger”* (repoPullBehavior setting):

* A *Requests Received badge* is shown on the Period List, indicating the number of pending downstream requests. Badge styling matches the Manual Upload request badge pattern.

* User clicks the badge to open the Requests Received modal.

* For each pending request, the modal shows the request details and a *“Fetch Data”* button (instead of the “Upload File” / “Create Period” buttons shown for Manual Upload sources).

* Clicking “Fetch Data” triggers the system to create a period for the requested date range (if needed) and immediately fetch data from the external system.

* The period appears in the Period List with refresh status *In Progress*.

* The success/failure outcomes follow the same rules as manual creation (AC14, AC15).

* *The system does NOT automatically fetch data.* It waits for the user to click “Fetch Data”.

h3. AC19: Cancel / Dismiss

* Clicking *Cancel* or the X close button closes the dialog with no period created and no fetch triggered.

h3. AC20: Access Control

* *Only users with data source management privileges* can access the Create Period dialog.

* The Create Period button is not shown to users without the required privilege.

h3. AC1: Entry Point — Upload File Button (Toolbar)

* The *"Upload File"* button is shown in the Period List toolbar for data sources with Manual Upload or Automatic Replication mode.

* The button is enabled when the data source is Active.

* The button is disabled with a tooltip when the data source is Inactive: *"Uploading is not permitted while the data source is Inactive."*

* Clicking the enabled button opens the Upload File side panel.

h3. AC2: Entry Point — Re-upload from Period Context Menu

* The period row context menu contains a Re-upload option.

* Clicking Re-upload on an Open period opens the dialog with the period pre-selected.

* Clicking Re-upload on a Locked period first shows a Locked Period Unlock Warning. Confirming opens the dialog; cancelling does nothing.
* The menu is disabled with a tooltip when the data source is Inactive: *"Re-uploading is not permitted while the data source is Inactive."*

h3. AC3: Entry Point — Upload from Requests Received Modal

* The Requests Received modal shows an *"Upload File"* button for each pending request for a new period or “Reupload File” button for each pending request for an existing period.

* Clicking it opens the Upload File dialog with period start and end dates pre-filled from the request.

* The date fields are read-only — the user cannot change them.
* The Upload or Re-upload buttons are disabled with a tooltip when the data source is Inactive.
* Clicking Upload or Re-upload on a Locked period first shows a Locked Period Unlock Warning. Confirming opens the dialog; cancelling does nothing.

h3. AC4: Period Selection — Existing Period

* When opened from the toolbar, the dialog shows a searchable list of existing periods in Mode A.

* The user can select any existing period to upload data into.

* A *"Add New Period"* button switches to Mode B (new period form).

h3. AC5: Period Selection — New Period

* In Mode B, the user can select a Period Type (Range or As-of) via dropdown.

* If the data source already has periods, the Period Type dropdown is disabled and locked to the existing type.

* Range type: shows Start Date and End Date fields using the shared date picker component.

* As-of type: shows a single As-of Date field using the shared date picker component.

* A *"Back to Existing Periods"* link returns to Mode A.

h3. AC6: Period Type Locking

* When the data source has existing periods, the Period Type field is disabled in the new period form.

* A helper text explains that the type is locked to match existing periods.

* The user cannot mix Range and As-of period types within the same data source.

h3. AC7: File Selection

* The file picker uses the shared file picker component.

* Accepted file types are restricted to the data source’s configured Data Format: *CSV*, *JSON*, or *XML*.

* If the selected file’s format does not match the data source format, an inline error is shown and the file is rejected.

* After a valid file is selected, the file name is displayed.

h3. AC8: Comments Field

* An optional comments field accepts free text up to 300 characters.

* Content is stored as part of the period’s notes.

h3. AC9: Duplicate Period Warning

* When the selected or newly created period matches an existing period’s date range, a confirmation modal appears.

* The warning states that existing data will be replaced.

* *"Proceed"* — upload continues, replacing existing period data.

* *"Cancel"* — returns to the dialog with no changes.

h3. AC10: Locked Period Unlock Warning

* When re-uploading to a Locked period (via context menu), a confirmation modal appears.

* The warning states the period will be unlocked.

* *"Proceed"* — period is unlocked and upload continues.

* *"Cancel"* — returns with no changes. Period remains Locked.

h3. AC11: File Parsing and Data Storage

* The system parses the file according to the data source’s format (CSV, JSON, or XML).

* The parsed records are stored as the period’s data set and preview data.

* The period’s record count is updated to reflect the parsed record count.

* The period’s last synced timestamp is updated to the current time.

* The uploaded file name is stored in the period’s notes alongside any user comments.

h3. AC12: Data Quality Validation

* After parsing, the system validates field consistency against previous periods.

* The system checks that columns required by linked downstream repositories are present.

* Quality issues are flagged on the period (quality badge updated) but do not block the upload from completing.

h3. AC13: Successful Upload — Toolbar / Re-upload

* On success, the dialog closes.

* The Period List updates: new period appears or existing period shows updated record count and sync timestamp.

* The period’s data quality badge reflects the result of the quality validation.

h3. AC14: Successful Upload — Request Fulfillment

* On successful upload triggered from a request, the corresponding period request is automatically marked as Fulfilled.

* The Requests Received badge count decrements.

* If no requests remain, the Requests Received badge disappears.

h3. AC15: Cancel and Dismiss

* Clicking *Cancel* or the X close button closes the dialog with no changes.

* No period is created or modified when the user cancels.

h3. AC16: Access Control

* *Only users with data source management privileges* can access the Upload File dialog.

* The Upload File button and Re-upload context menu item are not visible to users without the required privilege.

column363:
h3. AC1: Context Menu Option Display

* When a data source is *Active*, the context menu displays *"Deactivate"* with a destructive text treatment.

* When a data source is *Inactive*, the context menu displays *"Activate"* with a positive text treatment.

* The *"Deactivate"* and *"Activate"* options are mutually exclusive — only one is displayed based on the current active status.

* When the data source’s refresh status is *In Progress*, the entire context menu trigger button is disabled and not clickable.

h3. AC2: Deactivation Confirmation Modal

* When the user clicks *"Deactivate"*, a centered modal overlay appears with a backdrop.

* The modal title reads *"Deactivate Data Source?"*.

* The data source name is displayed below the title.

* A warning/caution icon is displayed above the title.

* The information panel contains three messages: (1) "All periods will be *locked*", (2) a critical warning that upload/refresh is blocked while inactive, (3) a note that data can still be viewed.

* Two action buttons are present: *"Cancel"* (secondary) and *"Proceed"* (primary).

h3. AC3: Deactivation Execution

* When the user clicks *"Proceed"* on the deactivation modal, the data source’s activeStatus changes from *Active* to *Inactive*.

* All periods belonging to the data source are set to *Locked* status, regardless of their previous state.

* The modal closes after confirmation.

* The list screen reflects the updated state immediately (badge, period counts).

h3. AC4: Activation Confirmation Modal

* When the user clicks *"Activate"*, a centered modal overlay appears with a backdrop.

* The modal title reads *"Activate Data Source?"*.

* The data source name is displayed below the title.

* A positive/informational icon is displayed above the title.

* The information panel contains two messages: (1) "Periods will remain in *Locked* state", (2) "Unlock the relevant periods to refresh or re-upload the data."

* Two action buttons are present: *"Cancel"* (secondary) and *"Proceed"* (primary).

h3. AC5: Activation Execution

* When the user clicks *"Proceed"* on the activation modal, the data source’s activeStatus changes from *Inactive* to *Active*.

* *No periods are unlocked.* All periods remain in their current Locked state.

* The modal closes after confirmation.

* The list screen reflects the updated state immediately (badge, menu item availability).

h3. AC6: Active Status Badge Update

* When activeStatus is *Active*, the badge displays "Active" with a positive visual treatment (green) and a colored dot indicator.

* When activeStatus is *Inactive*, the badge displays "Inactive" with a neutral/muted visual treatment (gray) and a gray dot indicator.

* The badge updates immediately after confirmation without requiring a page refresh.

h3. AC7: Period Count Update After Deactivation

* After deactivation, the *Periods (Open/Locked)* column in the list screen reflects: Open count = 0, Locked count = total number of periods.

* After activation, the period counts remain unchanged from the deactivated state (all still Locked).

h3. AC8: Manage Data Source Menu Gating

* When a data source is *Active*, the *"Manage Data Source"* menu item is clickable and navigates to the edit panel.

* When a data source is *Inactive*, the *"Manage Data Source"* menu item is disabled (grayed out, non-clickable).

* The disabled menu item displays a tooltip: *"Not permitted while the data source is Inactive. Activate the data source to make changes."*

h3. AC9: Cancel and Dismissal

* Clicking *"Cancel"* on either modal closes the modal with no state changes.

* The data source activeStatus and all period statuses remain unchanged after cancellation.

h3. AC10: Data Preservation

* After deactivation, all previously uploaded or imported period data remains intact and viewable.

* The *"Manage Periods"* menu item remains accessible for an inactive data source, allowing users to view historical period data.

* No period data is deleted, archived, or altered as a result of deactivation.

h3. AC11: Reversibility

* A data source can be deactivated and reactivated multiple times.

* Each deactivation locks all periods. Each subsequent activation does not restore the previous period state — periods must be manually unlocked.

h3. AC12: No Cascade to Downstream Repositories

* Deactivating a data source does not change the active status of any downstream repository linked to it.

* Downstream repositories continue to operate independently but may reflect stale or missing data from the deactivated source.

h3. AC13: Access Control

* *Only users with data source management privileges* can see and use the Activate/Deactivate menu options.

* Users without the required privilege do not see these options in the context menu.

column1: Modification of data source
column29:
As an Integration Admin with the Manage Data Sources privilege, I want to modify the configuration of an existing data source through a tabbed editing panel, so that I can update connection details, scheduling, admin assignments, and general information without recreating the source.

Attached the functional spec. Also, attached the prototype to production document which might be useful if we are using our prototype source code.
column363:
h3. AC1: Entry Point

* The *"Manage Data Source"* context menu item opens the Modify Data Source side panel for the selected source.

* The panel opens on the General Information tab by default.

* The panel is only accessible for Active data sources (disabled entry point for Inactive sources is covered in the Data Source List spec).

h3. AC2: Source ID is Read-Only

* The Source ID field is displayed as a disabled (read-only) field in the General Information tab.

* The value cannot be edited under any circumstance.

* No edit affordance (cursor, hover state) is shown on the Source ID field.

h3. AC3: Tab Navigation

* All four tabs are always visible: General Information, Connection Details, Schedule & Refresh, Assign Admins.

* The user can freely navigate between enabled tabs without saving.

* A red alert icon is displayed on a tab header when that tab contains validation errors, visible even when the tab is not active.

h3. AC4: Data Format Change — Flat File to Flat File

* When Data Format is changed between flat file formats (e.g., CSV to JSON), the Input Mode selector remains visible and the current Input Mode selection is preserved.

* No tab enable/disable changes occur.

h3. AC5: Data Format Change — Flat File to Relational

* When Data Format is changed to Relational (PostgreSQL), the Input Mode selector is hidden immediately.

* Refresh mode is locked to Automatic Import.

* Connection Details and Schedule & Refresh tabs become enabled immediately.

* This change takes effect in the UI without requiring Save.

h3. AC6: Data Format Change — Relational to Flat File

* When Data Format is changed from Relational to a flat file format (CSV, JSON, or XML), the Input Mode selector appears immediately.

* Input Mode defaults to *Manual Upload*.

* Connection Details and Schedule & Refresh tabs become disabled immediately.

* Existing connection configuration is preserved in memory (not deleted) in case the user switches back before saving.

h3. AC7: Refresh Mode Transition — Manual Upload → Automatic Import

* When Input Mode is changed from Manual Upload to Automatic Import, Connection Details and Schedule & Refresh tabs become enabled immediately.

* Connection fields become editable with existing values pre-filled (if previously configured).

* Manual upload ability will be disabled.

h3. AC8: Refresh Mode Transition — Manual Upload → Automatic Replication

* When Input Mode is changed to Automatic Replication, Connection Details and Schedule & Refresh tabs remain disabled.

* Schedule is auto-set to event-based (repository-triggered). No schedule configuration is required or shown.

* Manual upload ability will continue to be enabled.

h3. AC9: Refresh Mode Transition — Automatic Import → Manual Upload

* When Input Mode is changed from Automatic Import to Manual Upload, Connection Details and Schedule & Refresh tabs become disabled immediately.

* Existing connection and schedule configuration is preserved in memory but is not editable. It is excluded from the save payload when mode is Manual Upload.

* Manual upload ability will be enabled.

* New file format will be validated while uploading the source manually.

h3. AC10: Refresh Mode Transition — Automatic Import → Automatic Replication

* When Input Mode is changed to Automatic Replication from Automatic Import, Connection Details and Schedule & Refresh tabs become disabled immediately.

* Schedule is auto-set to event-based (request from repository), replacing any previously configured schedule.

* Existing connection config is preserved in memory but not editable.

* Manual upload ability will be enabled.

h3. AC11: Refresh Mode Transition — Automatic Replication → Manual Upload

* When Input Mode is changed from Automatic Replication to Manual Upload, Connection Details and Schedule & Refresh tabs remain disabled.

* The auto-set event-based schedule (request from repository) is cleared.

* Manual upload ability will continue to be enabled.

* New file format will be validated while uploading the source manually.

h3. AC12: Refresh Mode Transition — Automatic Replication → Automatic Import

* When Input Mode is changed from Automatic Replication to Automatic Import, Connection Details and Schedule & Refresh tabs become enabled immediately.

* The auto-set event-based schedule (request from repository) is cleared. Schedule reverts to time-based defaults. Connection fields become editable.

* Manual upload ability will be disabled.

 

h3. AC13: Tab Immediate Response

* Tab enabled/disabled state updates immediately when Data Format or Input Mode is changed — without clicking Save.

* When a tab becomes disabled due to a mode change, any existing validation errors on that tab are cleared.

* When the user switches back to a previously disabled tab’s compatible mode, previously entered values are restored in the form.

h3. AC14: Schedule — Enable Scheduled Import Toggle

* When *Enable Scheduled Import* is toggled ON, the Frequency, Run Time, Run Date (when applicable), and Timezone fields appear and are editable.

* When *Enable Scheduled Import* is toggled OFF, those fields collapse and are no longer visible.

* The Schedule Summary callout updates dynamically as schedule fields are changed.

* Run Date field is only shown when Frequency is not set to Continuous.

* Toggling the scheduled import OFF does not disable the On Repository Request section — those settings remain active.

h3. AC15: Schedule — On Repository Request Behaviour

* The *On Repository Request* section is always visible when the Schedule & Refresh tab is enabled (Automatic Import mode).

* Exactly one option must be selected: *Auto-pull from upstream system* or *Notify and manually trigger*.

* When Auto-pull is selected: the system automatically sends an API request to external source system and pull data when a downstream repository requests a period.

* When Notify and manually trigger is selected: the system sends a notification when a downstream request arrives and waits for manual API trigger action by authorized users having “Manage Data Source” privilege.

* This setting is independent of the Enable Scheduled Import toggle — it applies regardless of whether scheduled imports are enabled.

h3. AC16: Schedule — Concurrency Policy

* The *Concurrency Policy* dropdown offers three options: Allow, Forbid, Replace.

* Forbid: a new import run cannot start while one is already in progress.

* Allow: concurrent import runs are permitted.

* Replace: the current import run is cancelled when a new one is triggered.

h3. AC17: Assign Admins Tab

* The Assign Admins tab is always enabled, regardless of refresh mode.

* Selected admins show highlighted state with accent-coloured avatar initials and a check icon.

* When no admins are selected, a soft warning is shown: *"At least one admin should be assigned."* This does not block saving.

h3. AC18: Validation

* *Source Name* is required and must be unique across all data sources (excluding the current source).

* *Data Owner* is required.

* Connection Details fields are only validated when the Connection Details tab is enabled.

* Port and Connection Timeout must be numeric when Connection Details are enabled.

* Schedule fields have no required validation (all optional).

* Inline errors appear beneath the relevant field. A red alert icon appears on the affected tab header.

* Formats are validated when source files are uploaded manually.

h3. AC19: Successful Save

* Clicking *Update Source* saves all changes across all enabled tabs.

* lastModifiedBy is set to the current user and lastModifiedOn is updated to the current timestamp.

* Connection and schedule details are only included in the save payload when their respective tabs are enabled.

* The side panel closes on successful save.

* The data source row in the list screen updates to reflect name, refresh mode, and last modified timestamp changes.

h3. AC20: Cancel / Dismiss

* Clicking *Cancel* or the X close button closes the panel with no changes saved, at any point during editing.

* Unsaved changes to any tab are discarded.

h3. AC21: Access Control

* *Only users with data source management privileges* can access the Modify Data Source panel.

column1: Creation of data source
column29:
As an Integration Admin with the Manage Data Sources privilege, I want to register a new data source through a guided wizard, so that I can onboard external or internal data feeds into the integration platform with the correct connection, scheduling, and governance configuration.

Attached the functional spec along with screenshots. Also, attached the prototype to production document which might be useful if we are using our prototype source code.
column363:
h3. AC1: Wizard Entry Point

* When a user with the *Manage Data Sources* privilege navigates to the Data Sources list and clicks *"Create New"*, the system opens the Create Data Source side panel wizard.

* When a user without the Manage Data Sources privilege views the Data Sources list, the *"Create New"* button is not available.

h3. AC2: Step Counter Display

* The wizard header displays the current step number and total steps (e.g., "Step 1/4") with the current step name.

* When the user changes the Input Mode, the step counter total updates dynamically.

h3. AC3: General Information — Required Fields

* When Source ID is empty and user clicks "Next Step", an inline error *"Source ID is required"* appears below the field.

* When Source Name is empty, an inline error *"Source Name is required"* appears.

* When Data Owner is empty, an inline error *"Data Owner is required"* appears.

* When any validation error exists, a validation summary panel appears at the bottom of the step listing all errors.

h3. AC4: Source ID Uniqueness

* When the user enters a Source ID that matches an existing data source ID, the system displays *"Source ID must be unique"*.

* The wizard does not advance until a unique Source ID is provided.

h3. AC5: Source Name Uniqueness

* When the user enters a Source Name that matches an existing data source name, the system displays *"Source Name must be unique"*.

h3. AC6: Data Format — Input Mode Visibility

* When the user selects a flat file Data Format (CSV, JSON, or XML), the *Input Mode* radio card selection appears.

* When the user selects any other format (for example, Relational PostgreSQL), the Input Mode section is hidden and refresh mode defaults to Automatic Import.

h3. AC7: Dynamic Wizard Steps — Manual Upload

* When the user selects Manual Upload as Input Mode, the wizard shows 2 steps: General Information and Assign Admins.

* Connection Details and Schedule & Refresh steps are not shown.

h3. AC8: Dynamic Wizard Steps — Automatic Import

* When the user selects Automatic Import (or Relational format), the wizard shows 4 steps: General Information, Connection Details, Schedule & Refresh, and Assign Admins.

h3. AC9: Dynamic Wizard Steps — Automatic Replication

* When the user selects Automatic Replication, the wizard shows 2 steps: General Information and Assign Admins.

* The schedule is auto-configured as event-based, repository-triggered without any user input.

h3. AC10: Connection Details Validation

* When any required connection field (Connection Type, Host URL, Port, Database, Auth Method, Credentials Reference, Encryption, Timeout) is empty and user clicks "Next Step", the appropriate inline error appears.

* When Port is non-numeric, the error *"Port must be a number"* appears.

* When Timeout is non-numeric, the error *"Timeout must be a number"* appears.

h3. AC11: Credentials Security Warning

* The Credentials Reference field always displays a security warning: *"Do not enter raw passwords here. Provide reference to secure vault."* with a lock icon.

h3. AC12: Scheduled Import Toggle

* When the Enable Scheduled Import toggle is ON, the frequency, run time, run date, and timezone fields appear.

* When the toggle is OFF, the schedule configuration fields are hidden.

h3. AC13: Schedule Summary Display

* When scheduled import is enabled, the system displays a dynamic summary callout such as *"Data will be automatically imported daily at 02:00 AM (UTC)."*.

* The summary updates in real-time as the user changes frequency, time, or timezone values.

h3. AC14: Run Date Conditional Display

* When Frequency is Daily or Continuous, the Run Date field is not shown.

* When Frequency is Weekly or Monthly, the Run Date field appears.

h3. AC15: Repository Request Behavior

* The On Repository Request section displays two mutually exclusive radio card options: *"Auto-pull from upstream system"* and *"Notify and manually trigger"*.

* Default selection: Auto-pull.

h3. AC16: Admin Selection

* The Assign Admins step displays all available admin users as a selectable list.

* Clicking an admin toggles their selection state.

* Selected admins show accent avatar, bold name, and a checkmark icon.

* Default: "Admin" is pre-selected for new data sources.

h3. AC17: Admin Warning

* When no admins are selected, a warning message *"At least one admin should be assigned"* appears.

* The warning does not block creation — the user can still proceed.

h3. AC18: Successful Creation Defaults

* When a data source is created, it starts with Active status, Idle refresh status, 0 repository count, and an empty periods list.

* The createdBy, createdOn, lastModifiedBy, and lastModifiedOn fields are populated automatically.

h3. AC19: Panel Closes on Save

* When creation is successful, the side panel closes, new data source appears in the Data Sources list and users are navigated to the period view screen.

h3. AC20: Wizard Back Navigation

* When the user clicks *"Back"* on any step after Step 1, the wizard returns to the previous step with all form data preserved.

* On Step 1, the back button shows as *"Cancel"* and closes the panel.

h3. AC21: Panel Dismissal

* The user can close the panel via: the *X button* in the header, clicking the *backdrop overlay*, or clicking *"Cancel"*.

h3. AC22: Full Validation on Final Save

* When the user clicks "Create Data Source" on the final step, the system re-validates all steps (not just the current step).

* If earlier steps have errors, the wizard does not advance and errors are displayed.

h3. AC23: Automatic Replication Auto-Schedule

* When a data source is created with Automatic Replication mode, the schedule is automatically set to event-based with repository as the trigger source.

* No schedule configuration fields are shown to the user during creation.

h3. AC24: Concurrency Policy Options

* The Concurrency Policy dropdown offers three options: *Allow*, *Forbid*, and *Replace*.

* Default: Forbid.

column1: Properties panel synchronization
column29: The Properties panel stays synchronized with the currently selected fact and acts as the primary place for viewing and editing fact metadata. Whenever the user selects, deselects, updates, or removes a fact, the panel refreshes immediately to show the correct element, attributes, and validation details. When no fact is selected, the panel reverts to its empty or placeholder state.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

# Panel updates on:
#* Fact selection
#* Fact deselection
# Displays:
#* Element
#* Attributes
#* Validation status
# When no fact selected:
#* Shows placeholder state
# Updates occur instantly without refresh.

column1: Visual state transitions for facts
column29: The system visually communicates the lifecycle and status of each fact through distinct UI states. These states cover temporary selection, tagged fact, active macro tagging mode, incomplete fact, valid fact, and removed fact states. Each transition must be immediate, clear, and consistent so users can understand the exact status of the tagged content without ambiguity.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

# States include:
#* Selected
#* Tagged
#* Macro selection active
#* Macro tagging active
#* Incomplete
#* Valid
# Each state:
#* Has distinct visual style
# Transitions:
#* Immediate
#* No delay or flicker
# Visual consistency maintained across document.
column505: Text block and short string tagging

column1: Validate completeness of fact
column29: The system continuously evaluates whether each tagged fact contains the minimum required information to be considered complete. A fact remains incomplete until all mandatory fields, including at least the element name and reporting period, are populated. Incomplete facts are visibly flagged in the UI and counted in the tagging status indicators so the user can resolve them before finalization or export.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

# Fact incomplete if:
#* Element missing
#* Period missing
# Incomplete facts:
#* Visually flagged
# Status bar:
#* Displays count of incomplete facts
# Completing required fields:
#* Removes incomplete status immediately
column505: Text block and short string tagging

column1: Enforce data type validation during tagging
column29: When a user attempts to assign a taxonomy element to a text block fact, the system validates whether the selected element type is permitted for text block tagging. Only supported text-compatible data types can be applied. Invalid element types are rejected immediately, and the user is informed through an error notification while preserving the current fact state.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

# On element assignment:
#* System checks data type
# Allowed types:
#* All nonNumeric items
# Invalid types:
#* Action blocked
# Error notification displayed:
#* Clear and immediate
# Fact remains unchanged after rejection.

column1: Remove fact from macro boundary
column29:
Story Description:
User removes an existing fact tag from a macro boundary section by using the boundary-level remove action. The system clears the tagging association for the entire section, removes all related fact metadata from active state, and restores the section to its original untagged visual state without altering the underlying document content.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

# User clicks remove icon on boundary.
# Entire section loses tagged state.
# Fact record deleted.
# Boundary returns to original visual style.
# All attributes cleared.
# Content and formating preserved

# On removal:
#* Fact record removed from active list

#* Element

# Visual highlight removed immediately.

column1: Apply attributes to fact
column29: User configures attributes such as period, currency, scale, and additional metadata for a selected fact through the properties panel, ensuring the fact meets completeness and validation requirements.
column363:

# Attributes editable only when fact is selected.
# Available attributes include:
#* Period
#* Currency / Unit
#* Scale
#* Member
#* Footnote
#* Label Role
# Period:
#* Selectable via dropdown or picker
#* Must support valid reporting formats
# Currency:
#* Required for monetary elements
#* Dropdown provides valid options
# Scale:
#* Accepts predefined or numeric values
# Attribute updates:
#* Stored immediately in Fact record
# Favourite Settings:
#* Auto-fill attributes on element selection
# User can override auto-filled values.
# Invalid inputs trigger validation errors instantly.
# Values persist across navigation and reselection.

column1: Apply taxonomy element
column29: User assigns an XBRL taxonomy element to an existing fact using either drag-and-drop interaction or the properties panel, enabling semantic tagging of the selected content.
column363:

# Fact must be selectable.
# Properties panel activates upon fact selection.
# User can drag element from taxonomy panel:
#* Drop target highlights
#* Drop is accepted only on valid fact
# User can alternatively:
#* Search element in properties panel
#* Select from dropdown
# On element assignment:
#* Fact record updates with:
#** Element Name
#** Element Label
# UI reflects applied element immediately.
# If Favourite Settings exist:
#* Period auto-populated
#* Currency auto-populated (if applicable)
#* Scale auto-populated
# If no defaults:
#* Fields remain empty
# Reassigning element:
#* Replaces previous element
# No save action required; update is immediate.

column1: Boundary selection - Cancel macro tagging mode
column29: User exits macro tagging mode without completing the tagging process. The system reverts UI state and handles pending fact appropriately based on defined behavior.
column363:

# Clicking cancel:
#* Deactivates tagging mode
# Boundary color reverts to original.
# Icon resets to initial state.
# Pending fact:
#* Retained or discarded based on system rule (consistent behavior required)
# No element assigned during cancellation.
# UI shows no active tagging mode.

column1: Boundary selection - Tag entire macro boundary as fact
column29: User tags a complete macro section (such as a report section or notes block) as a single fact using the boundary control. The system groups all content within the section into one fact.
column363:

# Macro sections visually identifiable with boundary (e.g., green border).

#* Section type dropdown
#* Tag icon
#* Remove button
# Clicking “Tag this section” (tag icon):
#* Activates tagging mode
# Visual updates:
#* Boundary color changes
#* Icon toggles to “Cancel tagging mode”
# System creates Fact record:
#* Includes all content IDs in section
#* No element assigned initially
# Entire section treated as one fact.
# Properties panel reflects macro fact.
# Only one active tagging state per section.

column1: Manual Selection - Select arbitrary text and mark as Fact
column29: User selects any portion of document content (including words, sentences, paragraphs, or mixed structures such as tables and text) and marks it as a fact using the context menu. The system creates a pending fact record without assigning any taxonomy element or attributes, while visually indicating the tagged region.
column363:

#* Single word

#* Full sentence
#* Single paragraph
#* Multiple paragraphs
#* Combination of text and table cells

# Selected content initially shows default selection highlight.

#* Displays Fact context

# Multiple facts can be created independently.
# Fact persists across scrolling and navigation.
