column1: Borders and Shading Dialog – Borders Tab: "Automatic" Color Option Does Not Apply the Correct Automatic Border Color to the Document Across All "Apply to:" Contexts
column29:
*What "Automatic" means in the Color dropdown*

* "Automatic" is *not an RGB color*. It is a special reserved color token that instructs the application to resolve the border color automatically at render time.
* In the underlying OOXML document format, it is stored as {{<w:color w:val="auto"/>}} — not as a hex RGB value.
* It visually renders as *black* in the default document theme, but it is fundamentally different from explicitly selecting black ({{#000000}}).

*How it differs from selecting black explicitly*

* Explicit black stores {{w:val="000000"}} — a hardcoded RGB value that never changes regardless of theme.
* Automatic stores {{w:val="auto"}} — a dynamic token that resolves based on the document theme and context at render time.
* If the document theme changes, {{auto}} borders adapt; {{000000}} borders do not.

*What R5.0 must do when "Automatic" is selected*

* When the user selects "Automatic" and clicks OK, R5.0 must write {{w:val="auto"}} to the border color attribute in the generated OOXML — no RGB value should be written.
* If R5.0 is writing an explicit RGB (e.g., {{000000}}) instead of {{auto}}, that is a functional bug even if the visual output appears identical on screen.
* If R5.0 omits the color attribute entirely, that is also incorrect as it may cause inconsistent rendering across different viewers and themes.

*Why this matters for document fidelity*

* Documents edited in R5.0 and later opened in Word or other OOXML-compliant applications may render border colors incorrectly if {{auto}} is not honored.
* Round-trip fidelity between R5.0 and Word depends on this token being written and read correctly.

Count and Preserve Multiple Validation States for the Same Fact
column363:
h3. Acceptance Criteria

# A single fact can hold multiple validation states at the same time in Tagging Mode.
# When one fact has both an Error and a Warning, the Errors count increases by 1 and the Warnings count increases by 1.
# The same fact is visible in both filtered views when each corresponding metric is selected.
# Clicking the Errors metric highlights the fact if it currently has an Error, even when the same fact also has a Warning.
# Clicking the Warnings metric highlights the fact if it currently has a Warning, even when the same fact also has an Error.
# The system does not collapse multiple states on the same fact into a single combined status.
# Counts are maintained per validation state, not per fact record only.
# Removing the Error state from a fact that still has a Warning decreases the Errors count by 1 and leaves the Warnings count unchanged.
# After the Error state is removed, the fact no longer appears in the Errors filtered view.
# After the Error state is removed, the same fact continues to appear in the Warnings filtered view until the Warning is also resolved.
# Removing the Warning state from a fact that still has an Error decreases the Warnings count by 1 and leaves the Errors count unchanged.
# After the Warning state is removed, the fact no longer appears in the Warnings filtered view.
# After the Warning state is removed, the same fact continues to appear in the Errors filtered view until the Error is also resolved.
# When both the Error and Warning states are resolved for the same fact, the fact is removed from both filtered views and both counts are reduced accordingly.
# Real-time updates reflect each state transition immediately after the user edits the fact or its metadata.
# State removal for one validation type does not unintentionally clear any other active validation state on the same fact.
# The Properties Pane and document highlight behavior remain consistent with the remaining active state after partial resolution.
# If a fact has more than two simultaneous validation states, each applicable state is counted independently in its respective metric.
# The order in which states are resolved does not affect correctness of remaining counts.
# No duplicate counting occurs within the same validation state for the same fact unless the product explicitly treats separate violations of the same state type as separate countable items.

column1: Implement Validation Rules
column29: Enforce core XBRL validation rules, Dimension Rules, SEC EFM Rules and Inline XBRL Rules including duplicate detection, datatype checks, and period validation.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

* Duplicate fact detection works using concept, context, and unit.
* Conflicting value detection identifies mismatched values.
* Period type validation enforces instant vs duration.
* Data type validation enforces numeric/text rules.
* Error and warning messages match exact wording from spec table (page 3).

----

h2. Implement Dimension Rules

* Required dimensions are validated.
* Member-domain relationship is validated.
* Typed dimension structure is validated.
* Invalid combinations trigger errors with correct messages.

----

h2. Implement SEC EFM Rules

* Deprecated concept detection works.
* Anchoring validation works.
* Documentation label validation works.
* DEI validation works.
* Fiscal period validation works.

----

h2. Implement Inline XBRL Rules

* Transformation format validation works.
* Invalid formats trigger correct error message.



Below is the list of run time validations to be covered.



|Validation Source|Rule|Validation stage|Description|Trigger|System Response / Message|
|Core XBRL 2.1 rules|Check if same value is tagged with same concept, context, unit, and attributes. Pass = Warning|During tagging|Same concept + context + unit tagged multiple times|Tag applied again on same context|“Duplicate fact exists for same concept, context, and unit.”|
|Core XBRL 2.1 rules|Check if different values exist for same concept, context, unit, and attributes. Pass = Error|During tagging|Same concept/context but different values|Tag exists elsewhere with different value|“Conflicting values detected for the same fact.”|
|Core XBRL 2.1 rules|Check if concept periodType matches context period (instant/duration). Fail = Error|During tagging|Instant vs duration mismatch|Duration concept tagged with instant context|“Concept requires duration period.”|
|Core XBRL 2.1 rules|Check if fact value conforms to concept data type. Fail = Error|During tagging|Value not matching datatype|Text used for numeric concept|“Invalid data type for concept.”|
|Dimensions specification|Check if all required dimensions for a hypercube are present in context. Fail = Error|During tagging|Required dimension not provided|Table concept without axis/member|“Required dimension missing.”|
|Dimensions specification|Check if member belongs to the domain of the selected dimension. Fail = Error|During tagging|Member not in domain|Invalid axis-member combination|“Member not valid for selected axis.”|
|Dimensions specification|Check if typed dimension value follows expected XML schema/type. Fail = Error|During tagging|Invalid typed dimension value|Incorrect XML structure|“Invalid typed dimension value.”|
|Dimensions specification|Check if member is validly linked to domain via domain-member relationship. Fail = Error|During tagging|Member not linked to domain|Invalid relationship|“Invalid domain-member relationship.”|
|SEC EFM|Check if selected concept is marked deprecated. Pass = Warning|During tagging|Deprecated concept used|Old element selected|“Deprecated concept used.”|
|SEC EFM|Check if extension concept has anchoring. Pass = Warning|During tagging|Extension not anchored|Extension without anchoring|“Extension requires anchoring.”|
|SEC EFM|Check if extension concept has documentation label. Pass = Warning|During tagging|Missing documentation label|Extension element|“Documentation label recommended.”|
|Inline XBRL rules|Check if transformation format correctly converts value. Fail = Error|During tagging|Invalid transformation|Wrong ixt format|“Invalid transformation.”|
|SEC EFM|Check if mandatory DEI elements exist. Fail = Error|During tagging|Missing DEI tags|Missing EntityRegistrantName|“Required DEI element missing.”|
|SEC EFM|Check if fiscal period aligns with context. Fail = Error|During tagging|Wrong fiscal period|Incorrect FY/Q tagging|“Invalid fiscal period focus.”|

column1: Detect Calculation Errors (Mismatch)

* Matching values do not increment Errors.
* Each mismatched parent is flagged.
* Recalculation occurs instantly after value or relationship change.

column29: Detect and count critical validation issues such as datatype mismatches, rule violations, and conflicting values.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

* System identifies the errors on the facts based on the list of errors mentioned under [https://datatracks.atlassian.net/browse/R50-12376|https://datatracks.atlassian.net/browse/R50-12376|smart-link] 
* Each error on the fact increments the Errors count.
* Each error is associated with a specific fact/tag.
* Errors are recalculated immediately after any tag edit.
* Multiple errors on same fact are counted individually or as per defined logic (must be consistent).
* Error count reflects only current document state (no stale data).

column1: Refresh / Clear Filter Control
column29: Provide a control to clear active filters and reset document highlighting without affecting counts.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

* A refresh/reset icon appears on the validation bar.
* Clicking the control clears any active filter.
* After clearing, all document highlights are removed.
* The control does not reset counts, only filters.
* If no filter is active, clicking refresh does not cause errors.
* The control provides hover tooltip “Clear Filters”.
* The control is keyboard accessible.
* Visual feedback is provided on click (pressed state or animation).

column1: Display Validation Metrics with Icons and Counts
column29: Show Errors, Warnings, Incomplete, and Unapproved metrics with icons, counts, tooltips, and proper visual states.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

* Errors metric displays a red circular icon with an “X” indicator.
* Warnings metric displays an amber triangle icon.
* Incomplete metric displays a sky-blue information icon.
* Unapproved metric displays a gray check-circle icon.
* Each metric shows a numeric count next to the icon.
* Count updates visually without requiring page refresh.
* Metrics are aligned horizontally with equal spacing.
* Each metric has a clickable area that includes icon and count.
* Hovering over a metric changes cursor to pointer.
* Tooltip appears on hover explaining the metric definition.
* Metrics with zero count are still visible but visually de-emphasized.
* Metrics with non-zero count are visually emphasized.
* Icons and counts remain legible across zoom levels (80%–200%).

column1: Render Validation Bar at Top-Center
column29: Implement a floating validation bar positioned at the top-center of the document editor with proper styling, layering, and responsiveness.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

* The validation bar appears horizontally centered relative to the document viewport, not the browser window.
* The bar floats above document content and remains visible during vertical scrolling.
* The bar does not overlap critical editor controls (toolbar, menus).
* The bar uses backdrop blur styling and semi-transparent white background.
* The bar maintains consistent spacing and padding across screen sizes.
* The bar renders only on the XBRL mode and not in document editor mode.
* The bar renders immediately when the document editor loads.
* The bar does not flicker or shift position during document load or resize.
* The bar maintains z-index priority above document content but below modal dialogs.
* The bar width adapts dynamically based on number of metrics and screen width.
* The bar remains accessible via keyboard navigation (tab focus).
* Screen resizing does not distort icons or misalign text labels.

column1: Borders and Shading Dialog – Table Preview is Left-Aligned Instead of Center-Aligned
column29:
The Table Preview graphic inside the Preview panel on the Borders tab should be centered both horizontally and vertically within the preview container, matching the layout rendered by Microsoft Word.

column1: "0.25pt" Rule Thickness Missing from Width Dropdown in Borders and Shading Dialog (Borders & Shading Tabs)
column29:
The Width dropdown must include "0.25pt" as the minimum thickness value in both the Borders tab and the Shading tab. Word's full predefined width list includes:

* {color:#ff5630}*0.25pt*{color}

* 0.50pt

* 0.75pt

* 1.00pt

* 1.50pt

* 2.25pt

* 3.00pt

* 4.50pt

* 6.00pt

R5.0 must include "0.25pt" at the top of this list, consistent with Word.

* Bottom — distance from text (in points)

column1: Table Properties — 'Positioning...' button and Table Positioning dialog are not implemented when 'Around' text wrapping is selected
column29:
In R5.0's Table Properties dialog (Table tab), the 'Around' text wrapping option is present and selectable. However, when 'Around' is selected, no 'Positioning...' button appears alongside it. In Word, this button is critical — it opens the Table Positioning dialog, which provides full control over how a floating table is anchored and placed relative to surrounding content.

Without the Positioning dialog, selecting 'Around' text wrapping in R5.0 is non-functional: the table cannot be positioned, anchored, or configured as a proper floating object.

When 'Around' text wrapping is selected on the Table tab in Word, a 'Positioning...' button appears to the right of the Text Wrapping controls. Clicking it opens the Table Positioning dialog, which contains three sections:

# *_Horizontal_*

* Position — Specifies the horizontal placement of the floating table. Accepts either an absolute measurement (e.g. 0") or a named position:

◦  Left — aligns the table to the left margin

◦  Right — aligns the table to the right margin

◦  Center — centers the table horizontally

◦  Inside — positions the table toward the spine (for book layouts)

◦  Outside — positions the table away from the spine

* Relative to — defines the reference object for horizontal measurement. Options: Margin, Page, Column

# *_Vertical_*

* Position — Specifies the vertical placement. Accepts an absolute measurement (e.g. 0") or a named position:

◦  Top — aligns the table to the top of the reference

◦  Bottom — aligns the table to the bottom of the reference

◦  Center — centers the table vertically

◦  Inside / Outside — used for alternating-page layouts

* Relative to — defines the reference object for vertical measurement. Options: Margin, Page, Paragraph

# *_Distance from surrounding text_*

* Four independent fields controlling the gap maintained between the floating table and any text wrapping around it:

◦  Top — vertical gap above the table (Word default: 0")

◦  Bottom — vertical gap below the table (Word default: 0")

◦  Left — horizontal gap to the left of the table (Word default: 0.13")

◦  Right — horizontal gap to the right of the table (Word default: 0.13")

# *_Options_*

* Move with text — when checked, the table's vertical position is anchored to the paragraph it is associated with; if that paragraph moves, the table moves with it. When unchecked, the table is fixed to an absolute page position.

* Allow overlap — when checked, this floating table is permitted to visually overlap with other floating objects (tables, images, text boxes) in the document. When unchecked, floating objects reflow to avoid overlapping.

column1: Table Options — 'Allow spacing between cells' has no visual effect on the table
column29:
In R5.0's Table Options dialog, enabling 'Allow spacing between cells' and entering a spacing value (e.g. 0.5 in) produces no visible change to the table after clicking OK through both Table Options and Table Properties. The table renders identically before and after the setting is applied — no gaps appear between cells, and no structural change is visible.

In Microsoft Word, the same action produces an immediate and prominent visual change: each cell is rendered with its own independent border, and large, clearly visible gaps appear between all cells, matching the entered spacing value. The table structure is fundamentally restructured to reflect the spacing.

*Expected Behavior*

* After clicking OK, the table visually reflects the entered cell spacing — cells appear separated from each other with visible gaps matching the spacing value (0.5 in).

* Each cell is rendered with its own independent border, separated from adjacent cells by the specified spacing amount.

* Behavior matches Word: the table structure is restructured to show distinct cell gaps immediately upon OK.

column1: AutoFit menu is completely absent from the Layout tab — AutoFit Contents, AutoFit Window, and Fixed Column Width options are unavailable
column29:
In Microsoft Word, the Layout tab (Table Tools > Layout) exposes an AutoFit dropdown button that contains three column-sizing options:

 

# AutoFit Contents — resizes each column to fit its content width.

# AutoFit Window — expands the table to fill the available page/container width.

# Fixed Column Width — locks column widths at their current values, preventing automatic resizing.

 

In R5.0, the AutoFit menu is completely absent from the Layout tab. Users have no way to control automatic column sizing behavior for tables, which is a core table-formatting capability expected in any document editor claiming feature parity with Word.

*Impact*:
Users cannot control how table column widths are sized or constrained. This forces manual column resizing and prevents parity with core Word table-formatting workflows.

* AutoFit Window

* Fixed Column Width

 

Selecting each option should resize table columns as described:

* AutoFit Contents: Columns shrink or expand to match cell content width.

* AutoFit Window: Table stretches to fill the full page/container width.

* Fixed Column Width: Column widths are locked; content wraps within cells.

* The color change occurs immediately after tagging.
* The color persists until the tag is removed.
* Different states (valid vs incomplete) can reflect visually if applicable.
* The visual state does not interfere with selection highlights.

column1: Tag Cell via Drag-and-Drop (Lock State Enabled)
column29: Enable tagging using drag-and-drop when taxonomy is in lock state.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

* Dragging a concept from the taxonomy panel is enabled only when taxonomy is in lock state.
* Dropping the concept anywhere in the document applies it to the selected cell(s).
* The system correctly associates the concept with the active selection.
* Dropping outside valid areas does not apply the tag.
* Tagging works for both single and multi-cell selections.

column1: Navigate and Select Element from Taxonomy
column29: Allow users to select taxonomy elements through the properties pane.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

* Clicking on the “Element Name” field on the fact tab redirects to the main taxonomy tab.
* Users can switch between Main Taxonomy, Presentation tab and extension tab.
* Double-clicking an element from any of these tabs selects the element.
* The selected element fills the ‘Element name’ field and applied to the active cell or selection
* Navigation between taxonomy tabs does not lose current selection context.
* While on the element selection mode, if the user switches the navigation to document or any other area other than the main taxonomy closes the selection mode state.

column1: Activate Property Pane on Cell Selection
column29: Ensure that selecting a cell activates the properties panel with the correct context and tab.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria:*

* Selecting a cell automatically opens or updates the properties pane.
* The “Fact” tab becomes active when a cell is selected.
* This behavior occurs only when the taxonomy is not in lock state.
* The pane displays details corresponding to the selected cell.
* Switching between cells updates the pane content accordingly.

column1: Create and Manage Hidden Tags
column29: As an XBRL Tagger, I want to create and manage hidden facts — XBRL data points not visibly rendered in the document — so that I can capture required taxonomy disclosures that have no corresponding visible text in the filing.
column363:
h3. AC1: Create Hidden Fact Button Availability

* When the Properties panel is open with no document selection, the "Create Hidden Fact" button is displayed.

* When document content is selected, the "Create Hidden Fact" button is not shown.

h3. AC2: Standalone Hidden Fact Creation (Workflow 1)

* When the user clicks "Create Hidden Fact", a new hidden fact is created with isHidden: true.

* The Properties panel immediately activates for the new fact (selection.type === "hidden").

* Default values from Favourite Settings (period, currency unit, scale) are pre-populated.

* The element name field is empty; the fact appears in HiddenTagsPanel with "Incomplete" status.

h3. AC3: Free-Text Mode Indicator — Standalone Hidden Fact

* When the Properties panel is active for a hidden fact, the value field does not auto-populate from any document content.

* A violet banner displays the message "Hidden fact — type value manually".

* A keyboard icon appears in the value field area.

h3. AC4: Set Hidden Checkbox — Workflow 2

* When a tagged document element is selected, the "Set hidden" checkbox is visible and enabled.

* When the user checks "Set hidden", the fact's isHidden property is set to true.

* The value field switches to free-text mode; the keyboard icon and violet mode banner appear.

* The fact appears in HiddenTagsPanel immediately.

h3. AC5: Set Hidden Checkbox — Lock for Standalone Facts

* When the selection type is "hidden" (Workflow 1 standalone fact), the "Set hidden" checkbox is checked and disabled.

* A tooltip on the disabled checkbox reads: "Cannot uncheck — this is a hidden fact".

* No interaction with the checkbox is possible.

h3. AC6: Source Link — Standalone Hidden Fact

* When the Properties panel is active for a standalone hidden fact with no source link set, a "Source Link" row is shown with an "Associate to Content" button.

* When the user clicks "Associate to Content", source-linking mode activates.

* When the user clicks a document element in source-linking mode, the system captures the element ID and text as the source link.

* The Source Link row updates to display the captured source text (truncated to 6 words) and a Jump button.

* Change (edit icon) and Remove (trash icon) controls are shown alongside the linked source.

h3. AC7: Source Link — Document-Anchored Hidden Fact

* When a document-anchored fact (Workflow 2) is marked as hidden, the Source Link row shows the anchored document content (read-only).

* No change or remove controls are available for the source link in Workflow 2.

* A "Jump" button is present; clicking it scrolls the document to the anchored element and briefly highlights it.

h3. AC8: Value Auto-Fill Suppression for Hidden Facts

* When a source link is associated with a standalone hidden fact, the reported value field is not overwritten with the source text.

* Value entry remains manual regardless of the source link state.

h3. AC9: HiddenTagsPanel — Access and Empty State

* When the user clicks the Hidden Tags icon in the right sidebar toolbar, HiddenTagsPanel opens.

* When no hidden facts exist, the panel displays an empty state message: "No hidden facts yet" with guidance text.

h3. AC10: HiddenTagsPanel — Header Counts

* The panel header shows the total number of hidden facts (e.g., "4 total").

* The header shows the count of facts with "Ready" status (e.g., "2 ready").

* Counts update immediately when a hidden fact is created or deleted.

h3. AC11: Hidden Fact Card — Content Display

* Each hidden fact renders as a card with: status indicator dot, element name (or "No element" placeholder), role label (if element is mapped to a role), status badge, reported value, period, and currency unit.

* The status badge displays "Incomplete", "Missing Period", or "Ready" based on element name and period population.

* When an element name is not set, the badge shows "Incomplete" with an amber treatment.

* When an element name is set but period is not, the badge shows "Missing Period" with an amber treatment.

* When both element name and period are set, the badge shows "Ready" with a green treatment.

h3. AC12: Hidden Fact Card — Source Link Strip

* When a hidden fact has an associated source link, a source strip renders at the bottom of the card.

* The strip shows a link icon, the truncated source text (up to 5 words), and a "Jump" button.

* When the user clicks "Jump", the document scrolls to the source element and briefly highlights it in blue.

* When no source link exists, the source strip is not shown.

h3. AC13: Hidden Fact Card — Hover Actions

* When the user hovers a hidden fact card, a Manage icon (table grid) and a Trash icon appear.

* When the user clicks the Manage icon, ManageTagsPanel opens in hidden mode pre-selected to that fact.

* When the user clicks the Trash icon, an inline delete confirmation replaces the status badge on the card.

h3. AC14: Delete Confirmation Flow

* When the delete confirmation is shown on a card, "Confirm" and "Esc" buttons appear.

* When the user clicks "Confirm", the hidden fact and its tag are removed, and the card disappears.

* When the user clicks "Esc", the confirmation is dismissed and the card returns to its normal state.

* The fact's FactDetails record is deleted entirely (not reset) upon confirmation.

h3. AC15: Manage All Hidden Facts

* When the user clicks "Manage all hidden facts" in HiddenTagsPanel, ManageTagsPanel opens in hidden mode with no row pre-selected.

* The panel displays only facts where isHidden === true.

* When the user closes ManageTagsPanel, HiddenTagsPanel remains open and unchanged.

h3. AC16: ManageTagsPanel Row Click — Hidden Mode

* When the user clicks a row in the hidden-mode ManageTagsPanel, the Properties panel opens for that fact.

* The ManageTagsPanel closes when a row is clicked.

* The Properties panel reflects the correct hidden fact (selection.type === "hidden").

h3. AC17: Per-Card Manage to ManageTagsPanel

* When the user clicks the Manage icon on a specific hidden fact card, ManageTagsPanel opens in hidden mode.

* The specific fact row is pre-selected in the grid.

h3. AC18: Shell Tag Auto-Creation

* When a hidden fact is created via the Properties panel without a pre-existing tag, the system automatically creates a shell tag for it.

* The hidden fact appears in HiddenTagsPanel without any user action to create a tag.
* No duplicate shell tags are created if a covering tag already exists.

column1: Manage Tags — Hidden Mode
column29: _As a user, I want to view and manage all hidden facts in the Manage Tags table, so I can bulk-edit or review hidden XBRL facts efficiently._
column363:
*AC9.1* Opening Manage Tags from 'Manage all hidden facts' opens the panel with the title 'All Hidden Facts'.

*AC9.2* The table contains only facts where isHidden = true.

*AC9.3* All column, filter, sort, search, selection, bulk action, and export behaviors described in Stories 3–7 apply in Hidden Mode.

*AC9.4* Clicking a row for a hidden-only fact (no DOM anchor) opens the Properties panel rather than scrolling the document.

*AC9.5* The empty state message in Hidden Mode reads 'No hidden facts found.' when no facts match the current filter.

column1: Hidden Tags Panel — Card List
column29: _As a user, I want a dedicated panel showing all hidden facts as cards, so I can review their status at a glance and navigate to manage them._
column363:
*AC8.1* The Hidden Tags Panel is accessible from the right sidebar and shows a card for each fact where isHidden = true.

*AC8.2* Each card displays the concept name, role (if available from the presentation taxonomy), validation status badge, and linked source text (if any).

*AC8.3* The panel header shows the total hidden fact count and the count of 'Ready' facts (those with both elementName and period assigned).

*AC8.4* A 'Manage all hidden facts' button at the top of the panel opens Manage Tags Panel in Hidden Mode.

*AC8.5* Hovering a card reveals a per-fact 'Manage' icon; clicking it opens Manage Tags Panel for that specific fact.

*AC8.6* Each card has a delete action with a confirmation step before removing the tag.

*AC8.7* If there are no hidden facts, an empty state message is shown with guidance on how to create a hidden fact.

column1: Export CSV
column29: _As a user, I want to export the current filtered and sorted fact table to CSV so I can audit or share the tagging data outside the tool._
column363:
*AC7.1* Clicking the 'Export CSV' button generates a CSV file and downloads it to the user's browser.

*AC7.2* The exported file includes only rows currently visible after filters and global search are applied (not all rows in the underlying dataset).

*AC7.3* The exported file includes only columns currently configured as visible, in their current column order.

*AC7.4* The CSV header row uses the configured column labels.

*AC7.5* Values containing commas, double quotes, or newlines are properly quoted per CSV specification.

column1: Bulk Actions
column29: _As a user, I want to select multiple facts and take bulk actions (remove, approve, bulk edit) to efficiently manage large sets of tags._
column363:
*AC6.1* Each row has a checkbox for individual selection.

*AC6.2* The master checkbox in the table header selects all currently filtered rows when none are selected; deselects all when all are selected; is in an indeterminate state when some are selected.

*AC6.3* The Bulk Actions Bar appears between the panel header and the table only when at least one row is selected.

*AC6.4* The Bulk Actions Bar shows the count of selected facts (e.g., '3 facts selected').

*AC6.5* Clicking 'Remove Tags' removes the tags for all selected facts from application state and clears the selection.

*AC6.6* The 'Approve All' button is shown in the Bulk Actions Bar only when at least one selected fact has Pending approval state.

*AC6.7* Clicking 'Approve All' sets the approval state to Approved for all selected Pending facts; already-approved facts are not affected.

*AC6.8* Clicking 'Bulk Edit' reveals an inline form for setting Period, Unit, Scale, and Sign across all selected facts.

*AC6.9* Clicking 'Apply' in the Bulk Edit form applies only the fields that have been explicitly set; unmodified fields are not overwritten on the selected facts.

*AC6.10* After a bulk action completes, the selection is cleared.

column1: Search, Filter, and Sort
column29: _As a user, I want to search, filter per-column, and sort the fact table so I can quickly isolate specific facts for review._
column363:
*AC5.1* The global search input filters all visible rows using a case-insensitive substring match across all visible column values.

*AC5.2* Rows that do not match the search term are hidden; the table updates in real time as the user types.

*AC5.3* Clicking the filter icon on a column header opens the column filter popover with options to sort ascending, sort descending, clear sort, clear filter, and set a filter value.

*AC5.4* The Status, Approval, Method, and Hidden columns present dropdown filter controls with predefined options; all other columns present a free-text input.

*AC5.5* A column header with an active filter or sort shows a highlighted (blue-tinted) filter icon.

*AC5.6* The 'Clear All Filters' button appears in the header bar whenever any column filter is active; clicking it removes all column-level filters.

*AC5.7* Global search and column-level filters are applied together (AND logic); only rows matching both conditions are shown.

*AC5.8* Clicking a column label sorts by that column; a second click on the same column toggles direction; only one column is sorted at a time.

*AC5.9* The active sort direction is shown as an arrow icon in the column header.

column1: Column Resize and Reorder
column29: _As a user, I want to resize and reorder columns directly in the table header so I can customize the layout to my reading preferences._
column363:
*AC4.1* Each column header displays a resize handle at its right edge that becomes visible on hover.

*AC4.2* Dragging the resize handle changes the column width; the minimum width is 60px and cannot be dragged below it.

*AC4.3* Resizing does not affect other columns' widths.

*AC4.4* Column headers in the table are draggable; dragging a header to a new position reorders that column.

*AC4.5* While dragging a column header over a target column, the target column header receives a visual drop-indicator highlight.

*AC4.6* Dropping a header on the same position it started produces no change.

column1: Configure Columns
column29: _As a user, I want to show, hide, and reorder columns in the Manage Tags table so I can focus on the data most relevant to my current task._
column363:
*AC3.1* Clicking the Configure Columns button (sliders icon) opens the column configuration popover anchored to the panel's top-right area.

*AC3.2* The popover lists all available columns with their current order and visibility state (checkbox per column).

*AC3.3* Unchecking a column hides it from the table immediately.

*AC3.4* Re-checking a hidden column restores it to the table.

*AC3.5* The last visible column cannot be unchecked; the checkbox for the sole remaining visible column is disabled.

*AC3.6* Each column entry in the popover is draggable; dragging reorders the columns in both the table and the popover list.

*AC3.7* Clicking the Reset button restores all columns to default visibility and default order.

*AC3.8* Clicking outside the popover closes it without any additional action.

column1: View and Navigate Tagged Facts
column29: _As a user, I want to see all tagged facts in a structured table and click a row to navigate to the tagged content in the document or open its properties._
column363:
*AC2.1* Each tagged fact appears as one row in the table, with Status, Approval, Method, Hidden, Value, Element Name, Period, Unit, Scale and other default columns visible.

*AC2.2* Rows representing hidden facts (isHidden = true) are displayed with a visually distinct tinted background.

*AC2.3* Single-clicking a row for a standard (non-hidden-only) fact scrolls the document to the tagged content and updates the Properties pane to reflect that fact.

*AC2.4* Single-clicking a row for a hidden-only fact (ID begins with 'hidden-') opens the Properties panel for that fact rather than scrolling the document.

*AC2.5* Double-clicking any row opens the Properties panel for that fact, regardless of hidden state.

*AC2.5.1*  The user can double-click a tagged fact in the document editor. The system loads the relevant tags for the selected fact in the Manage Tags panel.

*AC2.6* The Status column correctly shows the validation state of each fact: Error (red), Warning (amber), Incomplete (blue), Valid (green).

*AC2.7* The Approval column shows 'Approved' for approved tags and 'Pending' for unapproved tags.

*AC2.8* The Method column shows AI or Manual per the tag's method field.

*AC2.9* An empty-state message is shown inside the table body when no rows match current filters (message text is context-aware: hidden / role / element mode).

*AC2.10* Any property change made in the Properties panel for a selected fact is reflected immediately in the corresponding Manage Tags row — with no save action, no refresh, and no delay. This includes: Element Name and Label Text updating when the element is changed; Period, Unit, and Scale columns updating when those fields are modified; the Approval badge switching from Pending to Approved when the fact is approved; the Hidden badge and row tint appearing when isHidden is toggled on; the Dimensions column updating when members are added or removed; the Footnote column updating when footnotes are linked or unlinked; the Sign column reflecting sign changes; and the row being removed from the table entirely when the tag is deleted. The same instantaneous reflect-back applies when a fact is restored from the History tab.

*AC2.11* Rows where two or more facts share an identical combination of Element Name, Period, Unit, and Members display a duplicate context warning indicator (‘!’ badge) inside the Status cell. The indicator is a visual warning only — it does not change the validation status, block approval, or prevent export. The badge recalculates automatically whenever the row data changes (e.g. after a period or unit is updated in the Properties panel).

*AC2.12* The Hidden column displays a violet ‘Hidden’ badge for any fact where isHidden = true, and a dash for all other facts. Hidden fact rows additionally receive a violet background tint across the full row width. Both the badge and the row tint update immediately when isHidden is toggled via the Properties panel — no row refresh is required.

column1: Open Manage Tags from Taxonomy
column29: _As a filer, I want to open Manage Tags from any element or role node in the taxonomy tree, so I can see all tagged facts for that element or section in one place._
column363:
*AC1.1* Click the context menu item labelled 'Manage Tags' available next to each element/Role in the Taxonomy Panel (Presentation tab).

*AC1.2* Selecting 'Manage Tags' on an element node opens the Manage Tags Panel in Element Mode; the panel title matches the element's label.

*AC1.3* The table is populated only with facts whose concept name matches the selected element.

*AC1.5* Selecting 'Manage Tags' on a role node opens the panel in Role Mode; the panel title matches the role label.

*AC1.6* In Role Mode, the table includes facts for all elements that are children (at any depth) of that role.

*AC1.7* The panel can be closed with the X button; closing it does not affect document state.

column1: Real-time ruler measurement does not show negative, positive, left, and right values during drag

column404:
When the user drags an indent marker or margin on the ruler, Word Desktop shows a live measurement tooltip. It shows the exact value in real time. It displays both positive values (movement to the right) and negative values (movement to the left). The values are precise — up to two decimal places (e.g., −0.63 cm). The user can also control the measurement unit (cm, inches, or points).

column1: Maintain UI consistency across taxonomy interactions
column29: Ensure UI reflects correct hierarchy and actions.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria*

* Context menus always show valid options based on node type.
* Taxonomy tree updates instantly after create/update/delete.
* Selected node context persists correctly during operations.
* No mismatch between Presentation and Extensions tab data.
* Modal always reflects correct parent context and type behavior.

column1: Remove extension element
column29: User deletes an extension from taxonomy.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria*

* Right-click or context menu shows “Remove” option.
* Clicking “Remove” opens confirmation dialog:
** Message includes element label
* If user cancels:
** No action taken
* If user confirms:
** {{onRemoveExtension(id)}} is triggered
* Element is removed from:
** Presentation tree
** Removed from the facts on the document
** Extensions tab
* No modal is opened during deletion.
* UI updates immediately after removal.
column449: Remove extension element - If values are tagged in the extended element, the system must first show that the element is in use. The user can remove the tagged values, then the system allows removing the element.

column1: Modal cleanup after save
column29: System resets modal state after completion.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria*

* Modal closes immediately after successful save.
* All internal states reset:
** Type → Monetary
** Period → Instant
** Balance → Not Applicable
** Abstract → false
* No previous values persist.
* Reopening modal starts fresh with default configuration.

column1: Update existing extension element
column29: System updates an existing extension.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria*

* Payload includes:
** Existing element ID
** Updated fields
* API handler {{Update Extension}} is triggered.
* Updated values reflect instantly in:
** Presentation tree
** Extensions tab
* No duplicate nodes are created.
* Only modified properties change.

column1: Create new extension element
column29: System creates and inserts a new extension into taxonomy.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria*

* Payload includes:
** All form fields
** parentId from context
* API handler {{Create Extension}} is triggered.
* New element appears immediately:
*# As child node under selected parent in Presentation tree
*# In Extensions tab list
* Element reflects correct hierarchy and type.
* If name was auto-generated:
** Final generated name is sent in payload.
* UI updates without requiring refresh.

column1: Validate mandatory fields before save
column29: System ensures required fields are filled before saving.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria*

* Clicking “Save Element” triggers validation.
* Mandatory fields:
** Element Label Text
** Element Name
** Other attribute validation based on the selected data type
* If any field is empty:
** Browser alert is displayed
** Save is blocked
* No API call is triggered on validation failure.
* Focus remains on modal for correction.

column1: Conditional field locking and enabling
column29: Fields become editable or locked based on selected type.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria*

* Locked fields appear visually disabled (greyed out).
* Locked fields cannot be clicked, typed into, or modified.
* Unlocking occurs only when switching to a type that allows editing.
* No partial locking inconsistencies occur.
* “Others” type unlocks all fields completely.
* UI feedback clearly differentiates editable vs non-editable fields.

column1: Balance field dynamic behavior
column29: Balance dropdown visibility and behavior depends on data type.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria*

* Balance field is visible only when Data Type = monetaryItemType.
* Switching to non-monetary types hides Balance field.
* When hidden:
** Value resets automatically to “Not Applicable”.
* Switching back to monetary:
** Balance field reappears.
** Default value is “Not Applicable”.
* User can select Debit or Credit only when visible.
column449: * User can select Debit, Credit, or *N/A* only when visible. In some cases, the extended element balance type should be N/A.

column1: Element Name auto-generation
column29: System generates element name dynamically from label input.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria*

* Typing in “Element Label Text” triggers real-time name generation.
* Conversion rules:
** Remove spaces and special characters
** Convert to PascalCase
** Example: “Cash and Equivalents” → “CashAndEquivalents”
* Name updates continuously as label changes.
* Name includes the label suffix
* If user manually edits Element Name:
** Auto-generation stops permanently for that session.
* Subsequent label changes do not affect manually edited name.
* No invalid characters appear in generated name.
column449:
Conversion rules: 

We accept removing spaces, but special characters must convert to words (e.g., & to and, numbers to words, <, >, and = to less than, greater than, and equal, % to percentage). 

We remove these special characters: (), -, _, @, superscript, ©️.

column1: Label suffix injection and management
column29: System auto-appends suffix to label based on selected type.
column363:

* Selecting a type appends suffix:
** Example: “[Axis]”, “[Table]”, “[Line item]”
* If label already contains a suffix from previous selection:
** Old suffix is removed before new suffix is added.
* Cursor is positioned immediately before suffix.
* User typing continues seamlessly before suffix.
* Manual editing does not break suffix formatting.
* Suffix remains consistent with current type at all times.

column29: User selects one of 11 extension types and sees dynamic configuration updates.
column363:

** *Custom* column (contexts where baseGroup = custom)
* Each column shows a *Search* field that filters the list by context label text.

** bold context label
** indicator: *(Duration)* or *(Instant)*
** a date summary line (From/To for duration; As at for instant)

*Hover actions in Standard column*

* When the user hovers over a context row in Standard, the system shows:
** *Edit* (pencil icon)
** *Delete* (trash icon)
* The user can click *Edit* on a context row to open the Period Mappings modal focused on that context.
* The user can click *Delete* on a context row to remove the mapping entry from the list and update totals accordingly.

*Custom column Add behavior*

* The user can click *Add* in the Custom column header.

column1: Configure Target Period and Live-Recompute Mappings
column29: Step 1 provides four live inputs that recompute all mappings immediately: fiscal year end, reporting period end, YTD toggle, and comparative data toggle.
column363:
*Target period input fields*

* The user can click the *Fiscal Period End Date* date field and select a date.
* The user can click the *Reporting Period End Date* date field and select a date.
* The user can click the *Year To Date* checkbox to toggle it on/off.
* The user can click the *Comparative Data* checkbox to toggle it on/off.

*Live recomputation*

* After the user changes any of the four inputs, the system recomputes mappings immediately (no save button required).
* The Standard and Custom columns update their date summaries to reflect the new computed results.

*YTD vs quarterly behavior*

* When *Year To Date* is checked, current-period duration mappings compute Start Date as *Jan 1 of the fiscal year* and End Date as the Reporting Period End Date.
* When *Year To Date* is unchecked, current-period duration mappings compute Start Date approximately *3 months before* the Reporting Period End Date (quarterly behavior), and End Date equals Reporting Period End Date.
* Current-period instant mappings always compute the instant date as the *Reporting Period End Date*.

*Comparative inclusion behavior*

* When *Comparative Data* is checked, comparative contexts compute by shifting dates *-12 months* from their current-period target mapping.
* When *Comparative Data* is unchecked, comparative contexts remain *unchanged* and display a “No change” status where applicable.

column1: Ensure Visual Highlights Work Consistently Across Table and Narrative Content
column29: Ensure that visual highlighting behaves consistently across different content types in the document editor.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# All tagging status highlights *must work consistently for narrative facts and table cell facts*.
# Highlighting *must remain visible during scrolling, zooming, and document navigation*.
# The system *must ensure that highlights do not interfere with text readability*.
# Highlights *must render correctly even when multiple facts are selected simultaneously*.
# The system *must maintain highlight consistency across editing, tagging, and review workflows*.

column1: Display Visual Highlights for Text Block Tagged Content
column29:
Provide clear visual highlighting for text block tagged content within narrative sections of the document. Text block tags may span single paragraphs, multiple paragraphs, multiple columns, or multiple pages when continuation tags are used. The system must visually represent the tagged content as a single logical fact while maintaining proper visual boundaries and continuity across the document layout.

The highlight must represent the entire tagged text block using a single continuous border, regardless of how the content flows across paragraphs, columns, or pages. The highlighting behavior must also correctly handle nested text block tags and continuation tagging scenarios.
column363:
h1. Acceptance Criteria

h2. Paragraph-Level Highlighting

# When a single paragraph is tagged as a text block, the system *must display a border highlight surrounding the entire paragraph*.
# The highlight *must enclose the paragraph as a single continuous visual boundary*.
# The highlight *must not break across inline formatting elements within the paragraph*.
# The highlight *must remain visible when the paragraph is not actively selected*.
# When the paragraph is selected, the system *must apply the selection highlight while preserving the tag highlight*.

----

h2. Multi-Paragraph Text Block Highlighting

# When a text block tag spans multiple paragraphs, the system *must display a single continuous border surrounding the entire group of paragraphs*.
# The highlight *must visually treat the entire tagged region as one logical unit rather than individual paragraph highlights*.
# The highlight *must include all paragraphs contained within the tagged block*.
# The highlight *must adapt dynamically if the document layout changes due to editing or reflow*.
# The highlight *must not introduce visual breaks between paragraphs that belong to the same text block tag*.

----

h2. Multi-Column Content Flow

# When text block tagged content flows across multiple columns within the page layout, the highlight *must visually continue from the end of the first column to the beginning of the next column*.
# The border highlight *must preserve the logical continuity of the tagged block even when the content spans across columns*.
# The highlight *must correctly wrap around column boundaries without overlapping adjacent content outside the tagged block*.
# The system *must ensure that the border rendering remains visually clear and readable within column layouts*.

----

h2. Multi-Page Continuation Handling

# When a text block tag spans multiple pages using continuation tags, the highlight *must close properly at the end of the page where the content ends*.
# The highlight *must resume at the beginning of the next page where the continuation content appears*.
# The highlight *must visually indicate that the content is a continuation of the same tagged fact*.
# The system *must ensure that the border highlight remains visually aligned with the tagged content across page boundaries*.
# The highlight *must maintain the same visual styling across all continuation segments of the text block*.

----

h2. Interaction with Continuation Tagged Content

# When a user selects any portion of a text block that contains continuation segments, the system *must highlight the entire tagged content across all pages*.
# The highlight *must activate simultaneously for all continuation segments of the tagged text block*.
# The system *must clearly indicate that the selected text block represents a single logical fact despite being distributed across multiple pages*.
# The system *must ensure that selecting a continuation segment does not isolate the highlight to that segment alone*.

----

h2. Nested Text Block Tag Handling

# When a large text block contains nested text block tags inside it, the system *must visually distinguish the nested tags from the parent tag*.
# Nested text block tags *must display a different border style or visual treatment from the parent text block*.
# When the parent text block is selected, the system *must highlight the full parent region while preserving the visual boundaries of nested blocks*.
# Nested text block borders *must remain visible inside the parent highlight*.
# The system *must ensure nested highlights do not overlap or obscure each other*.

----

h2. Highlight Consistency and Rendering

# The highlight *must remain visible during document scrolling, zooming, or navigation*.
# The highlight *must not obscure or distort the readability of the underlying text content*.
# The system *must update highlight boundaries dynamically when document layout changes due to editing or pagination changes*.
# The system *must ensure that the highlight rendering does not interfere with inline formatting such as bold, italic, links, or lists*.
# The highlight *must correctly adapt to different document layouts including single column, double column, and multi-page formats*.
# The highlight *must persist across editor refresh, navigation, and save operations*.

column1: Highlight for Facts Marked but Not Yet Tagged
column29:
Provide a visual indicator for content that has been marked as a fact but has not yet been tagged with taxonomy attributes. This state represents an intermediate step in the tagging workflow where the content has been identified as a fact but the tagging process has not yet been completed. The highlight must clearly distinguish this state from other tagging states such as incomplete tagging, approved tags, warnings, and errors.

This highlight must apply consistently to both narrative facts and table cell facts.
column363:
h1. Acceptance Criteria

h3. Fact Marked State

# When content is marked as a fact but no taxonomy element or tagging attributes have been applied, the system *must highlight the content using a purple visual border*.
# The purple border *must apply to both narrative facts and table cell facts*.
# The highlight *must remain visible when the fact is not currently selected*.
# The highlight *must visually distinguish this state from other tagging states such as approved tags, warnings, incomplete tagging, and error states*.
# The highlight *must allow the fact value or text content to remain clearly readable*.

----

h3. Selection Behavior

# When a fact marked in this state is selected, the system *must apply the selection highlight while preserving the purple fact-marked highlight*.
# The selection highlight *must not remove or override the purple border indicating the fact-marked state*.
# When the selection is cleared, *the purple border must remain visible*.

----

h3. Transition to Tagged State

# When a taxonomy element or tagging attributes are applied to the fact, the system *must replace the purple borer with the appropriate tagging state highlight*.
# The system *must update the highlight immediately when the fact transitions from marked state to a tagged state*.

----

h3. Consistency Across Content Types

# The purple fact-marked highlight *must behave consistently for narrative facts and table cell facts*.
# The highlight *must remain visible during scrolling, document navigation, and editing operations*.
# The system *must ensure that the highlight rendering does not interfere with document formatting or layout*.

----

h3. Interaction with Other States

# The fact-marked highlight *must not appear simultaneously with approved, warning, incomplete, or error highlights*.
# The system *must ensure that only one tagging state highlight is displayed for a fact at any time*.

----

h3. Rendering and Accessibility

# The highlight *must meet accessibility requirements for visual contrast and readability*.
# The system *must provide additional visual cues such as border or icon indicators if color alone is insufficient to distinguish the state*.
