column1: Handle Hidden HTML Tags and Inline Formatting Elements in Narrative Text Block Selection
column29:
h3. User story

* As a financial report user, when I select narrative text blocks, I want to ensure that hidden HTML tags and inline formatting elements are preserved so that the content remains well-formed and can be marked as a fact.

h3. Context

This issue focuses on the handling of hidden HTML tags and inline formatting elements in narrative text block selection. These elements are frequently used in financial reporting documents. It is crucial that the system maintains these elements during selection.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* The system must properly handle hidden HTML tags during narrative text block selection.
* Inline formatting elements must be preserved in the selected text.
* The presence of these elements should not compromise the HTML well-formedness.
* Content must be able to be marked as a fact without issues arising from hidden tags or formatting elements.

h3. Other information

N/A
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow narrative text block selections that include inline HTML formatting elements* such as {{<b>}}, {{<i>}}, {{<u>}}, {{<span>}}, {{<strong>}}, and similar inline markup.
# The system *must preserve inline formatting elements exactly as they appear within the selected narrative content*.
# The system *must allow selections containing hidden HTML elements used for document processing or XBRL handling*, including tags such as {{<ix:exclude>}}.
# The system *must ensure that hidden or inline HTML elements remain intact and are not removed or modified during the selection process*.
# The system *must include these elements as part of the selected HTML content when validating the selection for HTML well-formedness*.
# The system *must validate that the selected narrative content remains valid HTML even when hidden or inline tags are present*.
# If the presence of hidden or inline tags causes the selected content to become invalid HTML, the system *must prevent the content from being marked as a fact*.
# When such invalid content is detected, the system *must display the message:*
*“Selected content is not HTML valid to apply XBRL tag.”*
# When a valid narrative selection containing inline or hidden HTML tags is made, the system *must allow the user to initiate the “Mark as Fact” action from the right-click context menu*.
# The system *should retain the user’s selection after displaying a validation message so the user can review or modify the selection*.

column1: Support Narrative Text Block Selection Containing Embedded HTML Elements
column29:
h3. User story

* As a user, when I select narrative text blocks, I want to ensure that embedded HTML elements are preserved so that the content remains well-formed HTML.
* As a user, when I mark content as a fact, I want the system to validate the overall structure to ensure it is correct.

h3. Context

The issue involves enabling users to select narrative text blocks that include embedded HTML elements. This includes lists, tables, hyperlinks, and other structural HTML elements.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Users can select narrative text blocks that contain embedded HTML structures.
* The selection process preserves all embedded HTML elements.
* The system validates the overall structure of the selected content.
* The content must remain well-formed HTML before it can be marked as a fact.

h3. Other information

N/A
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow users to select narrative text blocks that contain embedded HTML elements* such as lists, tables, hyperlinks, and similar structured content.
# The system *must include embedded HTML elements within the selection when they appear inside the selected narrative block*.
# The system *must preserve the original HTML structure of embedded elements within the selected content*.
# The system *must ensure that selecting narrative blocks containing embedded HTML elements does not alter the structure or rendering of those elements in the document*.
# The system *must allow selections containing HTML elements such as ordered lists (*{{<ol>}}*), unordered lists (*{{<ul>}}*), list items (*{{<li>}}*), hyperlinks (*{{<a>}}*), and tables (*{{<table>}}*) when they are fully contained within the paragraph boundaries of the selection*.
# The system *must prevent the selection from breaking the structural integrity of embedded HTML elements* such as selecting only a partial list structure or partial table structure.
# If a selection partially intersects an HTML structural element, the system *must automatically adjust the selection boundaries to include the complete HTML element*.
# When a valid narrative block containing embedded HTML elements is selected, the system *must make the “Mark as Fact” option available in the right-click context menu*.
# Before marking the content as a fact, the system *must validate that the selected content remains valid and well-formed HTML*.
# If the HTML structure becomes invalid due to the selection, the system *must prevent the action and display the message:*
*“Selected content is not HTML valid to apply XBRL tag.”*

column1: Switch Between Cell Selection Mode and Inline Content Selection Mode
column29:
Enable users to switch clearly and predictably between two interaction modes within table content selection:

Cell Selection Mode, where the entire table cell is selected as a whole

Inline Content Selection Mode, where the user can select specific content within the cell

The system must ensure that single-click and double-click interactions behave consistently so users can easily move between selecting the full cell and selecting partial content inside the cell without confusion.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# A *single click on a table cell must place the system in Cell Selection Mode* for that cell.
# In Cell Selection Mode, the *entire cell must be treated as the selected unit*.
# In Cell Selection Mode, the *full cell must be visually highlighted* to indicate whole-cell selection.
# A *double-click on a selected or unselected table cell must switch the system to Inline Content Selection Mode* for that cell.
# In Inline Content Selection Mode, the system *must allow the user to place the cursor inside the cell content and select partial text or numeric content within that cell*.
# When Inline Content Selection Mode is activated, the system *must visually distinguish partial-content selection from full-cell selection*.
# Entering Inline Content Selection Mode *must replace the whole-cell selection state for that cell*, unless the product explicitly supports showing both states together.
# The system *must not require the user to use any separate toolbar action or menu option to switch from Cell Selection Mode to Inline Content Selection Mode* if double-click is the supported interaction.
# When the user completes a partial selection inside a cell, the system *must keep the cell in Inline Content Selection Mode until the user exits that mode*.
# Clicking once on another table cell while Inline Content Selection Mode is active *must exit Inline Content Selection Mode for the previous cell and activate Cell Selection Mode on the newly clicked cell*.
# Clicking outside the table while Inline Content Selection Mode is active *must exit Inline Content Selection Mode and clear any active partial selection*.
# Pressing *Esc should exit Inline Content Selection Mode* and return the cell to its default non-inline state.
# After exiting Inline Content Selection Mode, a subsequent single click on the same cell *must select the entire cell again in Cell Selection Mode*.
# The system *must ensure that switching between modes does not alter the underlying cell content, formatting, or table structure*.
# The system *should preserve intuitive user behavior by ensuring that single-click always prioritizes whole-cell selection and double-click always prioritizes inline content selection*.
# The system *should prevent ambiguous interaction states where the user cannot determine whether the cell or only partial content is currently selected*.
# Keyboard focus *should move appropriately when switching modes* so that users can continue selection actions without needing to reselect the cell.
# The mode transition *should work consistently for cells containing numeric values, textual values, mixed content, and parenthetical values*.

column1: Support Selection of Negative Values Represented Using Parentheses
column29: Enable accurate selection of negative numeric values represented using parentheses, which are commonly used in financial statements. The system must treat the entire parenthetical value as a single numeric value during content selection.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow users to select numeric values enclosed in parentheses* within table cells.
# When a user highlights a negative number formatted using parentheses (for example {{(1,000)}}), *the selection must include both parentheses and the numeric value*.
# The system *must treat parenthetical numbers as a single numeric value during selection* and should highlight the entire cell as one.
# If a user attempts to highlight only the numeric portion inside the parentheses (for example {{1,000}} inside {{(1,000)}}), the system *must automatically expand the selection to include the full parenthetical expression*.
# The system *must support parenthetical number selection regardless of numeric formatting*, including:
#* {{(100)}}
#* {{(1,000)}}
#* {{(1,000.50)}}
# The system *must support selection of parenthetical numbers even when they appear alongside other text within the same cell*.
# The selection *must visually highlight the entire parenthetical value when selected*.
# The system *must ensure that parenthetical values remain selectable through both drag-based selection and inline selection mode triggered by double-clicking the cell*.

column1: Prevent Invalid Partial Selection of Numeric Tokens Within Table Cells
column29: Ensure that when users select numeric values within a table cell, the system preserves the integrity of numeric tokens. Users should not be able to create selections that break the logical structure of a number (for example splitting thousands separators, decimal parts, or negative indicators). This prevents incorrect fact extraction when selecting numbers embedded within mixed content.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# When a user selects numeric content within a table cell, the system *must treat the numeric value as a single logical token*.
# The system *must prevent selections that split numeric formatting elements*, including:
#* thousand separators (e.g., commas or spaces)
#* decimal separators
#* negative indicators.
# If a user attempts to highlight only a portion of a number (for example selecting “1,0” from “1,000”), the system *must automatically adjust the selection to include the complete numeric value*.
# The system *must ensure that selection boundaries do not break numeric formatting structures* such as:
#* {{1,000}}
#* {{1 000}}
#* {{1,000.50}}
# When numeric values appear together with text inside the same cell, the system *must allow the number to be selected independently without requiring selection of the surrounding text*.
# The system *must maintain consistent selection behaviour for numbers regardless of whether they appear alone or embedded within text*.
# If the user attempts to highlight characters that partially intersect a number, the system *should snap the selection to the nearest valid numeric boundary*.
# The system *must ensure that numeric integrity is maintained during both drag-based and double-click-based selections*.

column1: Select Parenthetical or Partial Content Within a Table Cell
column29: Enable users to select specific content within a table cell when the cell contains multiple values or mixed content such as parenthetical numbers, annotations, or embedded text. While a single click should select the entire cell, users should be able to enter an inline text-selection mode within the cell using a double-click action. This allows the user to highlight only the required portion of the cell content for further actions such as marking the selected content as a fact.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# A *single click on a table cell must select the entire cell as a single selection unit*.
# When a cell is selected using a single click, *the entire cell must be visually highlighted* to indicate full cell selection.
# A *double-click on a table cell must activate inline content selection mode within the cell*.
# When inline selection mode is activated, the system *must allow the user to highlight specific characters or portions of text within the cell*.
# The system *must allow selection of parenthetical values inside a cell*, including values enclosed in brackets such as _(100)_.
# The system *must allow selection of numeric values that appear alongside other text within the same cell*.
# The system *must allow users to select partial content such as numbers, words, or phrases contained within the cell*.
# When partial content inside the cell is selected, *only the selected portion must be visually highlighted*, not the entire cell.
# The system *must support selecting numbers embedded in text strings within a cell* (for example: “Revenue (100)” or “Loss (200)”).
# Once a partial selection inside the cell is made, the system *must enable the contextual option "Mark as Fact" for the selected content*.
# The system *must ensure that the selection boundaries correspond exactly to the highlighted characters inside the cell*.
# The system *should allow users to adjust the selection boundaries within the cell by dragging the cursor*.
# If the user clicks outside the cell while in inline selection mode, *the system must exit inline selection mode and clear the partial selection*.
# The system *must ensure that selecting partial content within a cell does not modify the table structure or the surrounding cell content*.

column1: Select Narrative Numbers Embedded in Text
column29: Enable users to select numeric values embedded within narrative sentences.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow users to highlight numeric values embedded within narrative text*.
# Users *must be able to select only the numeric portion of a sentence without selecting surrounding text*.
# The system *must support numeric selections within sentences, paragraphs, and narrative sections*.
# The system *must allow selection of numbers containing formatting characters such as commas used as thousand separators*.
# The system *must allow selection of numbers containing spaces used as thousand separators*.
# The system *must allow selection of numbers that include currency symbols* (for example {{$}}, {{€}}, {{£}}).
# The system *must allow selection of numbers containing decimal values*.
# The selection *must precisely match the highlighted numeric characters* and must not automatically include unrelated surrounding text.
# The system *must prevent selections that partially break the structure of a numeric value*, such as selecting only part of a formatted number.
# If a user attempts to select only a partial segment of a number, the system *should automatically adjust the selection to the nearest valid numeric boundary*.
# Multiple numeric values appearing within the same paragraph *must be independently selectable*.
# When a valid numeric value is selected, the system *must make the “Mark as Fact” option available in the right-click context menu*.
# The *“Mark as Fact” option must only be enabled when a valid numeric selection exists*.
# If no numeric value is selected, the *“Mark as Fact” option must remain disabled or hidden*.
# When the user selects “Mark as Fact”, the system *must treat only the selected numeric portion as the target content for fact creation*.
# The system *must ensure that selecting and marking the numeric value as a fact does not modify the surrounding narrative text*.
# The system *should visually retain the selected numeric value until the user performs another selection or action*.
# The system *must allow users to adjust the numeric selection boundaries before invoking the “Mark as Fact” action*.

column1: Select Narrative Text Blocks
column29:
h3. User story

* As a user, when I select narrative content blocks, I want to ensure that I can select paragraphs or groups of paragraphs so that I can work with logically complete content segments.
* As a user, I want the system to enforce paragraph integrity when selecting multiple paragraphs so that I can maintain the structure of the narrative.
* As a user, I want the selected content to be validated for HTML well-formedness before marking it as a fact so that I can ensure the content is correctly formatted.

h3. Context

This issue involves enabling users to select narrative text blocks within a document. The selection must support structured paragraph-level boundaries to maintain logical completeness.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Users must be able to select narrative content blocks, including paragraphs and groups of paragraphs.
* The system must enforce paragraph integrity during the selection of multiple paragraphs.
* The selected content must be validated for HTML well-formedness before it can be marked as a fact.

h3. Other information

N/A
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow users to select a complete paragraph within the document as a narrative text block*.
# The system *must allow users to select multiple consecutive paragraphs as a single continuous text block selection*.
# When multiple paragraphs are selected, the *selection must begin at the start of a paragraph and end at the end of a paragraph*.
# The system must *allow selecting the content across multiple pages*
# The system *must prevent selections that start in the middle of a paragraph and end in the middle of another paragraph when selecting multiple paragraphs*. This should be allowed in single paragraph selection.
# If the user attempts to select content beginning or ending in the middle of a paragraph while selecting multiple paragraphs, the system *must automatically adjust the selection to align with full paragraph boundaries*.
# The selected narrative content *must be visually highlighted to clearly indicate the selected block*.
# The system *must preserve the original document structure and formating while performing the selection and must not alter paragraph formatting or layout*.
# When a narrative text block is selected, the system *must provide the option “Mark as Fact” in the context (right-click) menu*.
# The “Mark as Fact” option *must only become actionable when a valid text block selection exists*.
# Before marking the selected content as a fact, the system *must validate the selected content against HTML W3C standards to ensure that the content is well-formed and valid HTML*.
# The content selection *must not be allowed over existing boundaries* (by overlapping selection) but *can be selected within a boundery*.
# Selection should be allowed within an existing text block tag but not allowed the selection overlapping an existing text block tag.
# The HTML validation *must check for proper tag nesting, tag closure, and valid HTML structure within the selected content block*.
# Allow the user to mark the selected content as facts using “Mark as fact” option.
# If the selected content fails HTML validation, the system *must prevent the content from being marked as a fact*.
# When invalid HTML content is detected, the system *must display the message:*
*“Selected content is not HTML valid to apply XBRL tag.”*
# The system *should visually retain the user’s selection after displaying the validation message so the user can review or adjust the selection*.
# Once the user modifies the selection, the system *must revalidate the updated content before allowing the content to be marked as a fact*.
# The system *must ensure that validation occurs only on the selected content block and does not modify the underlying document HTML*.
# The system *should allow users to reattempt the action after correcting the selection without requiring the document to be reloaded*.

column1: Select Short String Content in Narrative Text
column29: Enable users to select short textual values directly within narrative content.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow users to highlight short text strings within narrative content using standard text selection actions*.
# The selection of short string could be
## Text within a single line
## Text from more than one line.
## Content starting middle of a line and/or ending middle of a line.
# The system *must support selection of single words, phrases, or short textual values*.
# The selected text *must be visually highlighted*.
# User must be able to mark the selected content as a fact using “Mark as fact” option available on the right click menu.
# The system *must support selection of alphanumeric text values*.
# The system *must support selection of dates or short textual descriptors*.
# The selection boundary *must precisely match the highlighted characters*.
# The selected text *must remain highlighted until the user changes or clears the selection*.
# The system must validate the selection using HTML W3C for valid html well formedness before marking a content as fact.
# Invlid content selection should prompt the user with the message “Selected content is not HTML valid to apply XBRL tag.”

column1: Select Non-Contiguous Table Cells
column29: Allow users to select multiple non-adjacent cells within a table.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow users to select multiple non-adjacent cells using Ctrl + Click (or equivalent multi-select modifier)*.
# Each selected cell *must remain highlighted as part of the selection group*.
# The system *must preserve previously selected cells while additional cells are selected using the modifier key*.
# The most recently clicked cell *must be treated as the active cell*.
# The system *must allow non-contiguous selections across different rows and columns*.
# The system *must support non-contiguous selection of both numeric and textual cells*.
# Clicking a cell without using the modifier key *must clear the previous multi-cell selection*.

column1: Select Cells Across Multiple Columns
column29: Allow users to select cells across multiple columns simultaneously.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow users to select cells across multiple columns by dragging horizontally across the table*.
# The selection *must include all cells across the selected column range*.
# The system *must visually highlight all cells included in the column selection*.
# The system *must support selections that span multiple rows across the selected columns*.
# The most recently clicked cell *must remain the active cell within the selection*.
# The system *must support column selections containing both numeric and textual content*.

column1: Select Cells in a Single Column
column29: Enable users to select multiple vertically aligned cells within a column.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow users to select cells vertically within a column by dragging the cursor upward or downward*.
# The system *must allow users to select a vertical range using Shift + Click between two cells in the same column*.
# All selected cells *must be visually highlighted*.
# The most recently clicked cell *must be treated as the active cell*.
# The system *must allow column selections covering any number of rows*.
# The system *must support column selections even when cells contain mixed content types*.
# The selection range *should dynamically update while the user expands the selection*.

column1: Select Multiple Cells Across Rows and Columns
column29: Allow users to select a rectangular range of cells across multiple rows and columns.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow users to select a rectangular range of cells by dragging from one cell to another across rows and columns*.
# The system *must include all cells within the rectangular boundary defined by the start and end points of the selection*.
# The entire selected range *must be visually highlighted*.
# The last selected cell *must be marked as the active cell*.
# The system *must support selections spanning multiple rows and columns simultaneously*.
# The selection highlight *must dynamically update while the user expands or reduces the selection range*.
# The system *must support selections containing both numeric and textual values*.
# The selection *must remain active until the user initiates a new selection or clears the existing selection*.

column1: Select Multiple Cells Within a Row
column29: Allow users to select multiple adjacent cells within the same table row.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow users to select multiple adjacent cells within a row by dragging across cells*.
# The system *must allow users to select a range of cells within a row using Shift + Click*.
# All selected cells *must be visually highlighted* as part of a continuous selection range.
# The most recently clicked cell *must be distinguishable as the active cell*.
# The selection *must include all cells between the start and end of the selection range*.
# The system *must support row selection even when cells contain mixed data types such as numbers and text*.
# Clicking outside the selection *must clear the existing selection*.
# Users *should be able to extend the selection range further within the row* using additional drag or Shift selection.

column1: Select Individual Table Cell Content
column29: Enable users to select a single cell within a table. The system should clearly indicate the selected cell and treat it as the active selection for further actions.
column363:
h2. Acceptance Criteria

# The system *must allow users to select an individual table cell* by single clicking directly on the cell.
# The selected cell *must be visually highlighted* using a selection indicator such as a border or background highlight.
# Only *one cell must be treated as the active cell* when a single selection is performed.
# When a user clicks another cell, the previous selection *must be cleared* and the newly clicked cell *must become the active selection*.
# The system *must allow selection of cells containing numeric values*.
# The system *must allow selection of cells containing textual values*.
# The selection functionality *must work consistently across all tables* regardless of table size.
# The selected cell *must remain highlighted* until the user changes the selection.
# The system *should support keyboard navigation using arrow keys* to move the active selection between cells.

column1: Taxonomy settings
Implement animated hover navigation for taxonomy and presentation tree nodes with hover action menu and icons
column29: As a user navigating the taxonomy or presentation tree, I want the hover state to move smoothly between tree rows and reveal row actions such as Manage Tags and the kebab menu (Three Dot Menu), so that navigation feels polished and important actions are easy to access without cluttering the tree.
column363:
*Acceptance Criteria*

# Each visible tree row in Taxonomy Tree and Presentation Tree is a hover target across its full row width inside the list container.
# On first hover, a light gray highlight appears on the hovered row with no delay.
# The hover highlight uses a flat visual style: background around rgba(0,0,0,0.05) to rgba(0,0,0,0.06), border radius around 6px, no shadow pop, no border-thickness change, no row expansion.When moving from one row directly to another, the same highlight layer moves mainly on the Y axis to the new row position. The row-to-row motion uses transform: translateY(...) and opacity only. Width, scale, font size, badge position, and shadow do not animate during hover transitions. Hover enter animation duration is 100ms. Row-to-row movement duration is 140ms. Hover leave animation duration is 100ms.
# The easing for the animated motion is cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1).
On pointer exit from the tree container, the highlight fades out quickly without dramatic slide-out behavior.
# In Presentation Tree, hovering a row reveals the Manage Tags action and the kebab / three-dot menu on the right side of the row.
# The Manage Tags and kebab / three-dot menu controls appear only for the hovered Presentation Tree row and do not remain visible for non-hovered rows unless already required by another state.
# Revealing the hover actions does not cause text jump, icon movement, badge shift, or row height change.
# The hover effect does not interfere with selected state, active state, drag-and-drop state, or context actions on the row.
# Clicking Manage Tags opens the tag management table for that node.
# Clicking the kebab / three-dot menu opens the options menu for that node.
